item.title: Crit Care: Predictive performance of bedside physiological parameters for the failure of prophylactic non-invasive ventilation after extubation
item.description:
Background: Extubation failure is associated with increased mortality. Whether bedside physiological variables can identify patients at risk of reintubation during prophylactic NIV after extubation is unknown.

Methods: In this post hoc analysis of a multicenter physiological study, 60 hypoxemic adults at high risk of extubation failure underwent two 1-hour NIV sessions after planned extubation, with oronasal and full-face masks in randomized crossover order. We assessed the magnitude of airway occlusion pressure (Pocc), the esophageal pressure swing (ΔPes), SpO₂/FiO₂, respiratory rate, tidal volume, dynamic lung elastance (EL,dyn), ROX index [(SpO₂/FiO₂)/respiratory rate] and the pressure-oxygenation index (POX, SpO₂/FiO₂ divided by Pocc). Prophylactic NIV failure was reintubation for respiratory failure within 7 days. Discrimination was assessed by ROC analysis.

Results: Fourteen patients (23%) experienced NIV failure. Pocc yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.83 (95% CI, 0.71-0.95) with the oronasal mask and 0.83 (95% CI, 0.72-0.95) with the full-face mask, showing greater discriminative performance than tidal volume (AUCs, 0.55 and 0.53), respiratory rate (0.54 and 0.38), SpO₂/FiO₂ (0.51 and 0.50), and the ROX index (0.54 and 0.38; all p < 0.05). By contrast, the discriminative performance of Pocc did not differ from that of EL,dyn (AUCs, 0.72 and 0.73; p = 0.08 and 0.11), POX (AUCs, 0.82 and 0.81; p = 0.68 and 0.29), or |ΔPes| (AUCs, 0.83 and 0.82; p = 1.00 and 0.64).

Conclusions: During prophylactic NIV, Pocc discriminated NIV failure better than conventional bedside variables, with no detectable difference from directly measured inspiratory effort. External validation is required.

item.title: Resuscitation: Total gastric and intragastric air volumes in immediate post-resuscitation whole-body computed tomography after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: Association with airway management, aspiration, diaphragmatic position and initial blood gas analysis
item.description:
Background: Gastric distension (GD) may occur during cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but quantitative human data after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remain limited. We quantified gastric volumes after OHCA and explored associations with prehospital airway strategy, CT-defined aspiration, diaphragmatic position, and initial blood gases.

Methods: This retrospective single-center study included OHCA patients undergoing post-resuscitation whole-body computed tomography (CT) within 180 minutes of emergency department (ED) admission between January 1, 2020, and March 31, 2025. Total gastric volume (TGV) and intragastric air volume (GAV) were quantified by CT volumetry.

Results: Of 255 identified patients, 120 underwent CT within 180 minutes. Median TGV was 594 mL and correlated strongly with GAV (p < 0.001). Among patients with an advanced airway at ED arrival, neither TGV (p = 0.20) nor GAV (p = 0.24) differed significantly between the tracheal airway (TA; n = 87) and supraglottic airway (SGA; n = 28) groups. CT-defined aspiration was numerically more frequent with SGA than TA (78.6% vs. 57.5%; OR 2.7; p = 0.071), whereas neither TGV nor GAV was associated with CT-defined aspiration. Weak positive correlations were observed between initial pCO2 and both TGV (ρ = 0.16; one-tailed p = 0.037) and GAV (ρ = 0.19; one-tailed p = 0.018).

Conclusion: Gastric volumes were high in this selected post-OHCA immediate CT (< 180 minutes) cohort. No significant differences were detected according to recorded prehospital airway strategy, and gastric volume was not associated with CT-defined aspiration. Mechanisms and clinical consequences remain uncertain and require prospective studies before preventive/ therapeutic implications can be established.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Time to methadone or buprenorphine initiation, remission without medications, and mortality among a clinical cohort of patients with HIV and OUD
item.description:
Background: People with HIV (PWH) and opioid use disorder (OUD) have poor HIV outcomes and higher mortality rates. Medications for OUD (MOUD) are guideline-recommended treatment for OUD. Because of their regular interactions with the healthcare system, PWH might have better access to MOUD than people without HIV, but real-world data on MOUD initiation among PWH is limited.

Objectives: To describe MOUD initiation in a cohort of PWH who were receiving outpatient HIV care in Baltimore, Maryland.

Methods: We included PWH with an OUD diagnosis between 2012 and 2024 who had any evidence of recent nonprescribed opioid use based on self-report, clinical documentation, or toxicology screening. We estimated cumulative incidence functions for MOUD initiation (based on self-reported methadone use and prescribed or dispensed buprenorphine) and assessed predictors of MOUD initiation.

Results: We included 234 PWH (65% male, 83% Black, median age of 49 years). Five years after the incident OUD diagnosis, 24% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 19%, 30%) had initiated buprenorphine and 12% (95% CI: 8%, 17%) had initiated methadone. Additionally, 23% (95% CI: 18%, 29%) had had no indication of ongoing nonprescribed opioid use for at least 12 months, 11% (95% CI: 7%, 15%) had died, 18% (95% CI: 14%, 23%) were lost to the clinic, and 11% (95% CI: 7%, 16%) remained engaged in HIV care and eligible for an MOUD. There were few strong predictors of MOUD initiation.

Conclusions: Overall, MOUD initiation was high in the cohort although more research is needed to further improve MOUD utilization.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Did the affordable care act keep patients out of the emergency department? Changes in Illinois, 2016-2024
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Objective: A central premise of the Affordable Care Act was that broader coverage would mean fewer emergency department visits. A decade later, has that happened? To address the need for longer term evidence, we describe changes in Illinois ED visits between 2016, two years after ACA Medicaid expansion, and 2024, after pandemic fluctuations in visit rates.

Methods: We conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of Illinois Hospital Association discharge data for ED visits in 2016 and 2024 by Illinois residents aged 18-64, the most insurance-sensitive age group. We analyzed visits by patient, hospital, and clinical characteristics, including ED visits for ambulatory care sensitive conditions (ACSC), as defined by the AHRQ Prevention Quality Indicators in ED Settings. Multivariable logistic regressions were used to estimate changes in the likelihood of an ACSC visit.

Results: Between 2016 and 2024, Illinois ED visits by residents aged 18-64 decreased from 3,168,399 to 2,653,154 (-16.3%). Visits identified as ACSC declined from 366,613 to 270,762, (-26.1%) with the largest decrease among the Medicaid-insured population. The odds of an ED visit for ACSC in 2024 compared to 2016 were lower for all patients (OR = 0.88 95% CI = 0.85-0.92). Decreases in odds were greatest for patients covered by Medicaid (17% lower) and Medicare disability (12% lower).

Conclusion: Declining ACSC visits, particularly among the Medicaid-insured, may reflect improved access to primary care. Insurance expansion is one part of the changing acute care delivery ecosystem, which includes increased telemedicine and urgent care centers as well as rising costs.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection without chest pain identified on a triage electrocardiogram
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an uncommon but potentially devastating cause of myocardial infarction (MI) that may present without chest pain, making the diagnosis challenging. SCAD differs from atherosclerotic MI in both mechanism and risk profile: it predominantly affects women in midlife with few traditional cardiovascular risk factors, and is associated with fibromuscular dysplasia, recent emotional or physical stressors, and pregnancy. This report describes a 74-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department (ED) for a gastroenterology referral without chest pain and was found to have anterior ST elevations from a distal left anterior descending artery dissection. Although her age, atherosclerotic risk factors, and absence of chest pain were atypical, her sex and anterior ST changes were characteristic of SCAD, and a preceding period of physical stress may have contributed. A triage ECG led to catheterization before her troponin resulted.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Follow-up of human papillomavirus positive patients after self-collection in the emergency department
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background: Emergency department (ED) patients often lack sufficient primary care access and are disproportionately under-screened for cervical cancer compared with the general population. The recent FDA approval of self-collection for HPV testing at healthcare sites may facilitate cervical cancer screening for some patients. Thus, we investigated the proposition that the ED presents an opportunity to engage otherwise hard-to-reach individuals with cervical cancer screening via in-ED self-collection for HPV testing. While HPV negative individuals do not require further screening, HPV positive individuals require additional steps in the outpatient setting to complete screening.

Objective: After recent completion of a feasibility study of HPV self-collection among eligible ED patients in which more than 80% of participants agreed to self-collect and approximately 75% successfully completed self-collection in the ED, we followed the individuals who tested positive for HPV to assess their rate of follow-up for outpatient completion of screening.

Methods: We conducted follow-up at 150 days via electronic health record review and telephone survey to determine the follow-up rate for individuals who tested positive for HPV after in-ED self-collection.

Results: Among the individuals who successfully completed self-collection for HPV in the parent study, 24 (15.9%) tested positive for HPV. At 150 days, 7 (29.2%) out of 24 had completed screening (1 additional participant had scheduled upcoming screening). Individuals with higher triage acuity were less likely to follow up for additional screening.

Conclusion: Additional supports are required to maximize follow-up for completion of screening among those who test positive after in-ED self-collection for HPV testing.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Financial Incentives and Inequalities in Dental Care Delivery
item.description:
Importance: Patients with no prior relationship with a National Health Service (NHS) general dental practice in primary care are less likely to successfully obtain a dental appointment compared with returning patients. As part of a post-COVID-19 pandemic NHS Dental Recovery Plan, a new patient premium (NPP) scheme was introduced in England from March 1, 2024, to encourage dental practices to treat patients who had not seen an NHS dentist in the past 2 years.

Objective: To assess whether the NPP scheme was associated with an increase in dental care utilization under the NHS.

Design, setting, and participants: This pooled cross-sectional study analyzed a national panel dataset of monthly dental activity data between March 2023 and March 2025 in England, using an interrupted time series approach with segmented regression analysis. All primary care practices that submitted claims for general dental services under the NHS were included.

Exposure: Implementation of the NPP.

Main outcomes and measures: Number of new dental patients, total number of dental patients, and units of dental activity delivered.

Results: A total of 4 377 699 new patients were seen under the NPP scheme; the mean (SD) count of adult patients was 235 380 (41 394) per month preintervention and 205 235 (18 950) postintervention, and of children was 140 502 (19 379) per month preintervention and 131 511 (14 752) per month postintervention. At the aggregate national level in England, there was no significant association between the NPP and the total number of new NHS dental patients. There was a monthly decline in new patients prior to (β, -76; 95% CI, -118 to -34) and at the point of (β, -665; 95% CI, -928 to -402) introduction of the NPP. There was a positive trend change after the NPP was implemented (β, 117; 95% CI, 58 to 175), driven primarily by an increase in the number of new adult patients and patients requiring band 2 and 3 treatments. Post-NPP trends varied across integrated care boards (ICBs). In ICBs where there was an increase in the number of new patients post-NPP, the total number of patients and dental activity delivered remained relatively constant or declined over time.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of all NHS dental practices in England, implementation of the NPP was associated with an increase in the number of underserved new patients, but results varied by geographical area. Findings suggested a potential substitution effect whereby new patients displaced returning patients under the NHS in the absence of a corresponding increase in dental capacity.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Applying Target Trial Emulation in Vaccine Research: A Scoping Review
item.description:
Importance: Target trial emulation (TTE) has emerged as a rigorous framework for strengthening causal inference in observational research, following the design principles of randomized clinical trials using clinical data. While TTE is increasingly applied in vaccine effectiveness and safety evaluations, its implementation, reporting practices, and alignment with regulatory standards for real-world evidence remain poorly characterized.

Objective: To evaluate the methodological rigor, reporting completeness, and regulatory alignment of observational vaccine studies that emulate a target trial.

Evidence review: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2021 and August 2025 that used clinical data to assess vaccine effectiveness or safety. Eligible studies explicitly or implicitly emulated a target trial through comparative, causal inference-based designs. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data on adherence to TTE core design components (ie, eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrasts, and analysis plans) and alignment with regulatory real-world evidence guidance.

Findings: Among 79 studies meeting inclusion criteria, 58 covered COVID-19, 19 covered influenza, and 12 covered other vaccine-preventable diseases, including herpes zoster, mpox, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and other diseases. Only 25 studies (31.6%) reported clearly documented protocols. Although most studies delineated eligibility criteria, exposures, and outcomes, validation of operational definitions was infrequent (eligibility: 4 studies [5.1%]; exposure: 4 studies [5.1%]; outcome: 14 studies [17.7%]). For bias assessment and mitigation, 61 studies (77.2%) explicitly defined time zero, a key step in reducing immortal time and selection biases, while 26 studies (32.9%) used negative control to assess residual bias and only 2 studies (2.5%) used quantitative bias analysis using E-values. Despite regulatory emphasis on data credibility, systematic data quality assessments appeared in only 5 studies (6.3%).

Conclusions and relevance: In this study, methodological rigor and transparency varied widely, with documented protocols, validated operational definitions, and systematic data quality assessments all uncommon. To improve reproducibility and regulatory credibility, future research should prioritize adopting standardized TTE reporting frameworks, ensure clearly documented protocols, and incorporate data quality assessments.

Dai H, Chang TY, He X, Eiden A, Wang WV, Cassell K

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Mistrust in Health Care Organizations Among US Adults
item.description:
Importance: Public trust in the health care system has declined for decades. Population-level mistrust and its demographic correlates are well-documented, but because most studies are cross-sectional, little is known about how individuals' mistrust changes over time.

Objective: To examine change in mistrust of health care organizations and to identify sociodemographic factors associated with these changes.

Design, setting, and participants: This longitudinal cohort study used data from a national probability sample of US adults (Ipsos KnowledgePanel) surveyed in 2021 and 2022. Data analysis was from March to April 2026. In 2021, 1449 of 2107 invited individuals (68.8%) responded, and in 2022, 1831 of 2756 (66.4%) individuals responded. Twelve individuals with missing data were excluded.

Exposures: Sociodemographic characteristics including gender, age, education, annual household income, self-rated health, race and ethnicity (categorized as Hispanic, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic White, and other), and political party.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was medical mistrust, assessed with the Medical Mistrust Index, which measures perceptions of health care organizations' honesty, fairness, and motives. Latent class analysis was used to identify classes of mistrust, and multinomial logistic regression was used to estimate associations of sociodemographic characteristics with mistrust class.

Results: Among 1437 participants (mean age, 48.6 [95% CI, 47.4-49.8] years; 51.9% [95% CI, 48.7%-55.1%] women), 4 mistrust statuses were identified at each time point, with similar probability distributions in 2021 and 2022 (strong mistrust: 0.32 vs 0.33; moderate mistrust: 0.33 vs 0.34; neutral: 0.15 vs 0.15; no mistrust: 0.20 vs 0.19). Despite this population-level stability, individual membership changed substantially; the probability of remaining in the same status was 0.26 for strong mistrust, 0.35 for moderate mistrust, 0.18 for neutral, and 0.22 for no mistrust. Non-Hispanic Black participants were less likely than non-Hispanic White participants to move from neutral to no mistrust status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.64), participants with a high school education were less likely than college graduates to move from strong mistrust to neutral (aOR, 0.36; 95% CI, 0.14-0.94), and participants leaning Democratic were more likely than those leaning Republican to move from neutral to no mistrust (aOR, 6.11; 95% CI, 1.20-31.19).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, most US adults reported at least moderate mistrust of health care organizations. Population distributions remained stable, yet most individuals moved between statuses, indicating that mistrust is dynamic rather than fixed. Differences in trust levels across demographic characteristics highlight the need to strengthen trustworthiness in health care systems.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Gestational Weight Gain and Mortality Among Children in Brazil
item.description:
Importance: Gestational weight gain (GWG) is a key indicator of maternal nutritional status and has been associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. However, evidence of the association of GWG with child mortality remains limited, particularly in low- and middle-income countries.

Objective: To examine the association between GWG and mortality among children younger than 5 years in Brazil.

Design, setting, and participants: This population-based cohort study used data from January 1, 2008, to December 31, 2020, from the 100 Million Brazilians Cohort, constructed through linkage of the Live Birth Information System, Food and Nutrition Surveillance System, and Mortality Information System databases, with statistical analyses performed between July and December 2025.

Exposures: GWG was defined as the difference between third trimester and prepregnancy weight and classified as below, within, or above the 2009 US Institute of Medicine guidelines and Brazilian references for GWG.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcome was neonatal mortality, postneonatal mortality, infant mortality, and mortality among children younger than 5 years. Adjusted hazard ratios (AHRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models controlling for maternal age, education, marital status, prenatal visits, prepregnancy body mass index (BMI), and year of birth. Analyses were stratified by prepregnancy BMI.

Results: Among 792 935 singleton live births from 2008 to 2020 (51.1% boys; 683 656 [86.2%] born to mothers aged 20-34 years), 6105 deaths occurred among children younger than 5 years (0.8%). Compared with GWG within the guidelines, GWG below the guidelines was associated with higher risks of neonatal mortality (AHR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.11-1.32), postneonatal mortality (AHR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.28), infant mortality (AHR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.11-1.27), and mortality among children younger than 5 years (AHR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.12-1.26). Women with underweight had the greatest AHR for mortality among children younger than 5 years (1.47; 95% CI, 1.10-1.96). GWG above the guidelines was not consistently associated with mortality.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, GWG below the guidelines was associated with increased early-life child mortality, particularly among women with underweight, highlighting the importance of monitoring maternal nutrition during pregnancy among vulnerable populations.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Mortality From Winter Storm Uri and Texas Power Outages Among Medicare Patients
item.description:
Importance: In February 2021, a severe freeze event and winter storm, together named Winter Storm Uri, caused widespread power outages across Texas, leaving millions vulnerable to record-breaking cold temperatures. The association of these events and the related power outages with population-level health outcomes is unclear.

Objective: To estimate the association of Winter Storm Uri and related power outages with mortality and hospitalizations among Medicare beneficiaries in Texas through a quasi-experimental design.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study used data on a 100% sample of Texas Medicare beneficiaries from 2019 to 2023. The week of Winter Storm Uri was defined as February 14 to February 20, 2021. Statistical analyses were carried out between August 2025 and June 2026.

Exposures: Winter Storm Uri and related power outages in February 2021.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was weekly county-level all-cause mortality in Texas counties among Medicare beneficiaries, compared with the change observed in the same counties in the following year. The secondary outcome was county-level all-cause hospitalizations, measured identically. Difference-in-differences regression models estimated excess mortality and hospitalization rates 4 weeks before and during the week of the storm. Analyses were repeated for the 4 weeks from storm onset. For both outcomes, subgroup analyses were stratified by power outage quartile and by characteristics for vulnerable populations.

Results: The main study sample comprised Texas counties with Medicare beneficiaries in 2021 (n=3 955 190; 50.2% aged 65-74 years; 54.1% female) and the main control sample comprised the same counties in 2022 (n=4 053 788; 49.9% aged 65-74 years; 54.1% female). During the week of Winter Storm Uri, weekly mortality increased by 2.94 (95% CI, 2.12-3.76) deaths per 10 000 beneficiaries. During the 4-week period from storm onset, excess mortality persisted, with 3.08 (95% CI, 2.72-3.44) excess deaths per 10 000 beneficiaries per week. Hospitalizations were not higher during the storm week; however, over the 4-week period from storm onset, hospitalizations were 2.04 (95% CI, 1.30-2.78) higher per 10 000 beneficiaries per week. Although there was widespread storm activity throughout the state, no increase in mortality was observed in counties with the fewest power outages, with 0.66 (95% CI, -2.16 to 3.48) excess deaths per 10 000 beneficiaries per week. Medicare beneficiaries with low income had the highest relative increase in deaths during the storm week, with 5.40 (95% CI, 2.82-7.99) excess deaths per 10 000 beneficiaries.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of Texas Medicare beneficiaries, Winter Storm Uri was associated with excess mortality and hospitalizations, particularly in counties with power outages and among Medicare beneficiaries with low income. These findings highlight the need for targeted public health and policy efforts to protect vulnerable Medicare populations from the growing health consequences of weather-related events.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Terminology Without Consensus: A Thematic Analysis of Nomenclature Choice and Program Structure Among Expanded EMS Programs in a Single State
item.description:
Objectives: Expanded emergency medical services (E-EMS) programs, such as mobile integrated health care (MIH) and community paramedicine (CP), are increasingly common in the United States (U.S.). Although an international consensus definition exists specifically for CP, the terminology used by active U.S. E-EMS programs is poorly described, yet has important implications for program visibility, stakeholder engagement, evaluation, and policy. We sought to characterize how E-EMS programs in a single state describe themselves and factors associated with their chosen terminology.

Methods: We conducted a qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with E-EMS programs in Ohio. We used "E-EMS" as a historically established, neutral umbrella term to avoid prespecifying MIH, CP, or MIH-CP terminology during program identification. We identified E-EMS programs through voluntary reports to Ohio EMS, the Emergency Triage, Treat, and Transport (ET3) roster, publicly reported E-EMS programs on national dashboards, and snowball sampling. An interviewee from each E-EMS program participated in a recorded semi-structured interview focused on E-EMS program terminology, goals, services, and partnerships. Interview transcripts were reviewed by two coders, with discrepancies discussed with and adjudicated by a third reviewer. We used an inductive approach to develop the codebook, followed by thematic analysis to identify themes and subthemes.

Results: We identified 58 E-EMS programs meeting inclusion criteria; 23 participated and were included in the analysis. Participants described inconsistent use and varying interpretation of common terms such as MIH, CP, or MIH-CP; one in four used alternative terminology (e.g., neighborhood paramedic, EMS outreach). Participants attributed their terminology choices to the variability in MIH definitions and to limited understanding of MIH or CP among patients or external stakeholders. Despite variation in program terminology, program goals were consistently focused on filling unmet community needs, and program services were uniformly described as adaptable and reliant upon partnerships outside of EMS.

Conclusions: The terminology used to describe E-EMS programs in a single state varied considerably. Despite this, E-EMS program goals and services were consistent, suggesting early convergence upon the core mission of E-EMS programs. Participants perceived inconsistent or unfamiliar terminology as a barrier to patient awareness, referral generation, and stakeholder engagement.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: More Than a Tobacco Problem: Cigarette Smoking as a Marker of Poorer Cardiovascular Health Among Emergency Medical Services Clinicians
item.description:
Objectives: Emergency medical services (EMS) work demands physical capacity, sustained alertness, and performance under stress, making cardiovascular health a workforce concern, not only a personal one. Cigarette smoking persists in portions of the EMS workforce, but whether it signals cardiovascular risk beyond tobacco exposure itself is unknown. We examined whether cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across the non-tobacco domains of the American Heart Association's Life's Essential 8 (LE8) framework among nationally certified EMS clinicians.

Methods: We conducted an observational study and cross-sectional secondary analysis of a voluntary survey offered to nationally certified emergency medical technicians (EMTs), advanced EMTs, and paramedics upon completion of recertification (October 2023-April 2024). To isolate associations beyond tobacco exposure, the primary outcome was a modified composite score (mLE7) averaging the seven non-nicotine LE8 domains (0-100 scale). Ideal cardiovascular health was defined as mLE7 ≥ 80. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models adjusted for demographic, educational, occupational, and organizational characteristics.

Results: Among 36,436 survey respondents, 7,703 had complete data for smoking status and all seven non-nicotine domains. Of these, 48.8% had never smoked, 45.2% formerly smoked, and 6.0% currently smoked. Mean mLE7 scores were 59.2 among never smokers, 56.9 among former smokers, and 51.5 among current smokers. Compared with never smokers, current smokers had lower adjusted mLE7 scores (β, -6.02; 95% CI, -7.63 to -4.41) and lower odds of ideal cardiovascular health (aOR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.23 to 0.61). Former smokers had intermediate results (β, -1.62; 95% CI, -2.37 to -0.87; aOR, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.62 to 0.86). Current smoking was associated with poorer scores across diet, physical activity, sleep, blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose domains (p < 0.05). Clinicians at private and hospital-based agencies had lower adjusted mLE7 scores than those at fire-based agencies.

Conclusions: Among EMS clinicians, current cigarette smoking was associated with poorer cardiovascular health across nearly every non-tobacco domain, suggesting that smoking may serve as a readily identifiable marker of broader cardiovascular risk in this workforce. Agencies may consider pairing cessation support with broader cardiovascular health initiatives for clinicians who smoke. Sensitivity analyses addressing missing data yielded consistent results.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Frequency of On-Scene Goal-Directed Field Interventions for Pediatric Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest in a Regional System of Care
item.description:
Objectives: Early on-scene resuscitation improves outcomes from pediatric non-traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA); however, for pediatric patients, the early evacuation strategy remains commonplace. We sought to determine the frequency of goal-directed interventions initiated by paramedics prior to transport for pediatric patients with OHCA in a regional emergency medical services (EMS) system.

Methods: In this retrospective observational study and cross-sectional analysis, we analyzed the Cardiac Arrest Registry to Enhance Survival (CARES) and linked electronic patient care reports (ePCR) data for patients aged <15 years treated by EMS for nontraumatic OHCA in Los Angeles (LA) County from January 2021 to December 2022. The primary outcome was the frequency of goal-directed therapies administered on scene prior to transport, which we defined as defibrillation for shockable rhythms and administration of epinephrine and fluid resuscitation for non-shockable rhythms. We also tabulated descriptive statistics regarding arrest characteristics, scene times, frequency of other prehospital treatments, and patient outcomes.

Results: Among 176 eligible pediatric OHCA cases analyzed in CARES, 112 (64%) were male, the median age was 10 months (IQR 3-51), and 162 (92%) had an initial non-shockable rhythm. Of these, 156 patients were successfully linked to electronic patient care report (ePCR) records for analyses of prehospital interventions. Among 143 patients with non-shockable rhythms, EMS administered epinephrine before transport in 58 (41%) and fluids in 12 (8%). Among 13 patients with shockable rhythms, EMS delivered defibrillation before transport in 11 (85%). Bag-valve-mask (BVM) use was documented in 80 (51%) patients, although its timing relative to scene departure could not be determined. Median on-scene time was 10 minutes (IQR 5-18). Ten patients (6%) survived to hospital discharge, including 6 (3%) with a favorable neurologic outcome.

Conclusions: In this regional EMS system, fewer than half of patients with non-shockable rhythms received a dose of epinephrine and fewer than one in ten received intravenous fluids prior to transport, whereas most patients with shockable rhythms were defibrillated on scene. Further work is needed to identify barriers to timely delivery of on-scene resuscitative interventions.

item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
Rationale: Obesity is associated with poor asthma outcomes. GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists induce weight loss and dampen airway inflammation independent of pathways currently targeted by biologics.

Objective: To compare differences in respiratory outcomes and weight loss between GLP-1-based medications and tezepelumab in asthma patients without diabetes.

Methods: A retrospective study was performed in a multi-institutional electronic health record database. Patients with specialist-treated, obesity-associated, moderate-to-severe asthma with at least one severe exacerbation in the prior year who initiated liraglutide, semaglutide, tirzepatide, or tezepelumab between January 1, 2022 and December 31, 2025 were identified. Prevalent diabetes was excluded. Patients were followed for subsequent exacerbations, rescue inhaler prescriptions, respiratory-related healthcare encounters, and time to greater than 10% loss in body mass index. Overlap weighting accounted for imbalance in baseline asthma and obesity characteristics.

Results: 2779 patients were identified, of whom 133 initiated liraglutide, 1770 semaglutide, 472 tirzepatide, and 404 tezepelumab. In weighted estimates, patients starting tirzepatide experienced a lower hazard of severe exacerbation compared to tezepelumab (weighted hazard ratio [wHR] 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.24-0.70); those starting semaglutide had a similar hazard (wHR 0.99; 95% CI 0.70-1.39). Tirzepatide and semaglutide initiators attained >10% reduction in BMI sooner, had less need for rescue inhalers, and had fewer subsequent respiratory-related encounters compared to tezepelumab.

Conclusions: GLP-1-based medications, and in particular dual-incretin GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists, may have comparable effectiveness to biologic therapy among patients with associated obesity without diabetes. Clinical trials are necessary to validate findings in this observational study.

item.title: Crit Care: Discordant evidence on corticosteroids in sepsis: a meta-research study
item.description:
Background: Despite an extensive evidence base of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews (SRs), current sepsis guidelines provide only weak recommendations for corticosteroid therapy, while available SRs report conflicting mortality conclusions. We aimed to characterize the evidence landscape of SRs evaluating corticosteroids for sepsis, including their clinical scope, underlying RCT evidence bases, mortality conclusions, and to explore potential sources of discordance.

Methods: Meta-research study of SRs on corticosteroids in sepsis published between 2015 and 2025. Study-pool overlap was assessed using a SR×RCT inclusion matrix, Jaccard similarity (J), and hierarchical clustering. SRs and RCTs were classified according to standardized Population, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome (PICO) profiles. We explored discordance in short-term mortality conclusions among clinically comparable SRs and potential associations with study-pool composition, target populations, and methodological characteristics.

Results: Forty-two SRs including 121 unique RCTs were identified. More than half of pairwise SR comparisons shared no RCTs, and only three pairs showed high overlap (J > 0.8). SRs addressing similar intervention and target population profiles frequently relied on different study pools. Among 38 SRs with short-term mortality meta-analyses, 15 (39%) reported benefit and 23 (61%) no evidence of effect. Discordance occurred exclusively among SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies; conclusions were consistent for hydrocortisone plus fludrocortisone (benefit) and hydrocortisone, ascorbic acid, and thiamine (no evidence of effect). SRs including adult sepsis ± shock populations more frequently reported benefit than those restricted to septic shock (62% vs 22%), although this comparison was based on only 22 SRs evaluating broad, non-specific corticosteroid strategies and estimates were imprecise. No single methodological or clinical factor consistently explained discordance.

Conclusions: SRs addressing apparently similar clinical questions frequently synthesized different underlying evidence bases and reported discordant conclusions. When selecting SRs to inform clinical decisions and recommendations for sepsis management, clinicians and guideline developers should consider not only methodological quality and reported PICO, but also whether the included RCTs adequately represent the intended clinical question.

item.title: Crit Care: BEYOND PICS: a conceptual framework for post-ICU recovery stewardship
item.description:
As survival from critical illness improves, the global burden of post-intensive care syndrome (PICS) and PICS-family continues to grow, reshaping the goals of modern intensive care. Despite growing awareness, prevention, follow-up and rehabilitation remain fragmented, and important gaps persist in the organisation of recovery-oriented care. We propose BEYOND PICS, a conceptual framework for ICU survivorship built around six complementary pillars: Begin before ICU discharge, Early follow-up and equitable access, Your journey, Ongoing multidomain assessment and rehabilitation, Networked care, and Driving improvement. Rather than describing clinical interventions to be implemented in practice, the framework promotes a coordinated recovery pathway integrating prevention, patient partnership, education, rehabilitation, multidisciplinary collaboration and continuous quality improvement across the peri-ICU continuum. BEYOND PICS is not a clinical bundle or guideline, it provides a mental model to guide the organization of care, integrating the key components of ICU survivorship into a coherent continuum of care while highlighting priorities for future research.

item.title: Crit Care: Family members' experiences of death and organ donation in intensive and critical care units: a qualitative systematic review with thematic synthesis
item.description:
Family members of patients in intensive care units (ICUs) occupy a uniquely distressing position, navigating death determination and organ donation decisions at the most acute moments of loss. Qualitative evidence on these experiences has predominantly focused on donation after brain death (DBD), leaving the distinctive challenges of donation after circulatory death (DCD) largely unexplored, with no synthesis to date attending to both pathways within a single review. This review aimed to synthesise qualitative evidence on family members' experiences of death determination and organ donation in intensive and critical care settings across both DBD and DCD pathways. Thematic synthesis was employed, incorporating reciprocal translation from meta-ethnography and constant comparison from grounded theory, following the Thomas and Harden three-stage analytical framework. Reporting adhered to the Enhancing Transparency in Reporting the Synthesis of Qualitative Research (ENTREQ) guidelines. Five databases were searched in December 2025 with no date restriction. Eligible studies were peer-reviewed qualitative or mixed-methods publications reporting verbatim family member accounts of death determination or organ donation in adult ICU settings. Quality was appraised using the CASP checklist and the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Twenty-eight studies (2001-2025; 14 countries) were included. Of the 28 studies, 13 addressed DBD exclusively, four addressed DCD exclusively, and eight examined both pathways. Three analytical themes emerged. "Constructing Death" pertains to how families make sense of death determination through suspended temporality, bodily witnessing, and contested definitions, processes differing markedly between pathways. "The Contested Body" encompasses tensions between bodily sanctity and organ donation, shaped by clinician behaviours and consent processes. "Relational Meaning-Making" regards how families construct meaning through collective deliberation, cultural and religious frameworks, and farewell rituals. Whilst both pathways share core experiential dimensions, DBD families navigated the sensory dissonance of a physiologically supported yet neurologically dead loved one, whilst DCD families faced temporal compression and the moral weight of perceived involvement in an irreversible clinical event. Family experiences are simultaneously individual, relational, and culturally embedded. Findings point to context-sensitive practice considerations, communication quality, person-centred care, and institutional flexibility, that may support families across both DBD and DCD contexts.

item.title: Crit Care: A pilot study of circulating DPP3 and renin to identify high-risk phenotypes and mortality in septic shock
item.description:

Rapid identification of patients at risk for worse outcomes and/or targeted therapeutics are needed. item.title: Chest: Bedside ECMO Cannulation by Intensivists and Emergency Physicians
item.description:
The number of centers capable of initiating extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for critically ill patients with refractory cardiac or respiratory failure is expanding. Historically, patients were taken to the operating room or catheterization laboratory for ECMO cannulation by cardiothoracic surgeons and perfusionists. More recently, non-surgeons who have undergone specialized training are performing percutaneous ECMO cannulation and initiation of support at the bedside at some centers. This approach is attractive, in part, because of the timely initiation of ECMO and avoidance of the risk of patient deterioration during transport to a procedural area. The purpose of this article is to provide a roadmap for intensivists and emergency physicians to lead ECMO bedside procedures including veno-venous (VV), veno-arterial (VA), and hybrid veno-arteriovenous (V-AV) cannulation at ECMO-capable centers. These procedures demand cognitive and technical skills that are already foundational to critical care practice, including vascular access guided by point-of-care ultrasound and leadership during a dynamic resuscitation. A team-based approach to bedside ECMO cannulation is presented and illustrated with figures and video, including preparation, procedural execution, subsequent patient management, and programmatic considerations such as training and credentialing requirements.

item.description:
Background: The use of veno-venous extracorporeal life support (VV-ECLS) for severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) has increased substantially worldwide. However, approaches to liberation from extracorporeal support remain poorly defined, with no standardized protocols or validated readiness criteria.

Research question: What are the global practices for VV-ECLS liberation among Extracorporeal Life Support Organization (ELSO) centers? Where is there variability in readiness assessment, liberation strategies, and use of standardized protocols?

Study design and methods: We formulated a cross-sectional survey of 25 questions regarding liberation practices among ECLS providers. Questions focused on assessed parameters for readiness to liberate, determination of liberation success, and strategies to optimize it. Surveys were distributed electronically to 765 institutions globally registered with ELSO between July 1st and Aug 15th, 2022. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize responses.

Results: Of 765 centers contacted, 340 (44%) responded, with 209 (61%) reporting use of VV-ECLS. Most centers were adult-focused, intensivist-led programs with moderate annual volumes. Most respondents (58%) prioritized VV-ECLS liberation before liberation from mechanical ventilation. Readiness for liberation was most determined by improvement in oxygenation under lung-protective ventilation (92%) and respiratory system compliance (90%), while fewer centers used inspiratory effort indices (34%). Liberation strategies were heterogeneous, with progressive reduction of sweep gas flow being most common (40%). Liberation trial duration varied widely (median 120 minutes; mean 497 ± 635 minutes), and most centers performed one trial per day. Arterial blood gas abnormalities (90%) and clinical signs of respiratory distress were the primary indicators of liberation failure. Only 42% of centers reported using a formal liberation protocol.

Interpretation: VV-ECLS liberation practices vary substantially across centers and are largely guided by institutional experience rather than standardized evidence. These findings highlight the need for validated physiologic predictors and protocolized strategies to optimize safe and timely liberation from VV-ECLS.

item.title: Lancet: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research
item.description:
Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

item.title: Lancet: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial
item.description:
Background: The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa.

Methods: This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing.

Findings: The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia).

Interpretation: SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Serum lactate distribution across neurologic emergencies: implications for seizure identification

item.description:
Background: Serum lactate is routinely measured in emergency departments (EDs) as a marker of systemic metabolic stress, but its distribution across neurologic emergencies is poorly characterized. We evaluated serum lactate distributions among patients with suspected neurologic emergencies and its utility for seizure identification.

Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 22,430 consecutive ED visits and identified 637 ambulance-transported patients with suspected neurologic emergencies. All underwent venous blood gas analysis and non-contrast computed tomography on arrival. Serum lactate levels were compared among seizure (SZ), cerebral infarction (INF), transient ischemic attack (TIA), subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH), and other diagnoses. Multivariable logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and classification and regression tree (CART) analyses were performed.

Results: Serum lactate differed significantly across diagnostic groups (P < 0.001) and was highest in patients with SZ and SAH. Among patients evaluated for ischemic stroke, age and serum lactate independently predicted SZ. ROC analysis showed moderate discrimination between SZ and ischemic stroke (INF/TIA) (area under the curve, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.90). CART identified 4.05 mmol/L as the primary lactate threshold, with age providing additional stratification. Patients with lactate ≥4.05 mmol/L and age < 59.5 years had a 100% probability of SZ.

Conclusions: Serum lactate shows distinct distributions across neurologic emergencies encountered in the ED. Although not disease-specific, age-adjusted interpretation of serum lactate may improve seizure identification in patients presenting with suspected stroke. Because lactate measurement is rapid and routinely available, it may provide practical support for early diagnostic decision-making.

item.title: Am J Emerg Med: Activated partial thromboplastin time following Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® reversal of apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin: a propensity-score matched cohort study
item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background: Kcentra® and Balfaxar® are the four-factor prothrombin concentrates (4F-PCCs) available in the United States. Both contain heparin to prevent in-vial activation, but Balfaxar® contains approximately 2-10 times more heparin versus Kcentra®. Activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is commonly used to monitor heparin activity. This study compared aPTT changes following administration of Kcentra® versus Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, and warfarin reversal.

Methods: This single-center, retrospective, propensity-score matched cohort study included adults given Kcentra® or Balfaxar® for apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin reversal. Patients had a baseline aPTT and a repeat aPTT within eight hours after 4F-PCC administration. Patients were matched 1:1 based on baseline aPTT and 4F-PCC dose. The primary outcome was aPTT change following administration. Secondary outcomes were hemostatic effectiveness within 24 h, new thrombotic events within seven days, and all-cause mortality within seven days.

Results: A total of 1026 orders were screened, of which 46 patients had a 4F-PCC order meeting inclusion criteria and 30 were successfully matched (15 in each group). There was not a statistical difference between groups for hemostatic effectiveness, new thrombotic event, or all-cause mortality, but the CIs for the between-group differences were wide.

Conclusion: In this small propensity-score matched cohort of patients treated with apixaban, rivaroxaban, or warfarin, Kcentra® and Balfaxar® were not associated with significantly different changes in aPTT despite their markedly different heparin content. No statistically significant between-group differences were identified for hemostatic effectiveness, thrombotic events, or all-cause mortality, but the wide CIs preclude any conclusion of clinical equivalence. Larger studies focusing on patient-oriented outcomes are needed.

item.description:
Background: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion in the emergency department (ED) may occur during prolonged ED stays. We evaluated hospital stay and recurrent ED use among adults with severe anemia.

Methods: This retrospective cohort included ED encounters at a single tertiary academic hospital in Poland from January 2025-June 2026 with first hemoglobin <8.0 g/dL. Exposure was recorded ED RBC administration. Hospitalized encounters underwent propensity-score overlap weighting and patient-clustered bootstrap. Missing endpoints and available vital signs were recovered. Sensitivity analyses included 50 imputed datasets and weighted medians.

Results: Among 131,711 ED encounters, 1381 met eligibility criteria; 742 involved ED RBC transfusion. The hospitalized cohort included 610 encounters (175 with and 435 without ED RBCs). The adjusted total stay difference among survivors was 10.9 h (95% confidence interval [CI], -42.5 to 65.8); downstream estimates remained imprecise. ED stay was 9.4 h longer (95% CI, 8.0-10.8). Among 341 patients with transfusion followed by direct discharge, recurrent patients generated 52.1% of 541 episodes; 31.7% returned within 30 days.

Conclusions: Hospitalized encounters with recorded ED RBC administration had longer ED stays; treatment-related time could not be separated from waiting for inpatient beds. Downstream estimates allowed benefit or harm. Neither causal effects nor equivalence can be inferred. Pathways for stable recurrent anemia warrant evaluation while preserving urgent ED transfusion.

item.title: JAMA: Plasma eMTBR-tau as a Biomarker for Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy Tau Tangle Neuropathology
item.description:
Importance: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease that cannot accurately be diagnosed during life due to the absence of in vivo biomarkers for CTE neuropathology.

Objective: To evaluate plasma endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau (eMTBR-tau) as a candidate biomarker for CTE tau tangle neuropathology.

Design, setting, and participants: This case series included 21 former American-style football players who completed a blood draw as part of participation in clinical research at Boston University beginning April 17, 2008, and who subsequently died, donated their brain, and had completed autopsy by October 9, 2026.

Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau nucleic acid-linked immunosandwich assay single-plex immunoassay and plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) (SP-X n = 20; Elecsys n = 1).

Main outcomes and measures: CTE status and stage. Cumulative neuropathologic tau burden scores ranged from 0 to 33 (higher scores indicate tau burden; 0, no tau burden).

Results: Among 21 male brain donors (median age at blood draw, CTE positive: 68 years [IQR, 61-77]; CTE negative: 49 years [IQR, 47-56]), 18 had a neuropathologic diagnosis of CTE. Of these participants, 16 had a diagnosis of high-stage CTE (stage IV = 8, stage III = 8); and 2, of low-stage CTE (stage II = 1, stage I = 1). Five CTE-positive participants had intermediate or high Alzheimer disease neuropathologic change (ADNC). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in CTE-positive participants (median, 0.019 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.030]) compared with CTE-negative participants (0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.61 [95% CI, 0.51-2.70]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentrations were highest among CTE-positive participants with comorbid ADNC (0.082 pg/mL [IQR, 0.059-0.131]) and intermediate among those with high-stage CTE without ADNC (n = 11; median, 0.009 pg/mL [IQR, 0.004-0.021]). Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was significantly higher in high-stage CTE (median, 0.021 pg/mL [IQR, 0.006-0.038]) compared with low-stage CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.002]; β = 1.79 [95% CI, 0.45-3.13]) or no CTE (median, 0.001 pg/mL [IQR, 0.001-0.001]; β = 1.78 [95% CI, 0.85-2.71]). Differences remained significant after exclusion of 5 cases with comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau concentration was associated with higher cumulative neuropathologic tau burden score across 11 brain regions (β = 0.71 [95% CI, 0.38-1.05]). Plasma p-tau217 concentration was positively associated with eMTBR-tau (β = 0.68 [95% CI, 0.32-1.04]) but was not associated with CTE. P-tau217 concentrations were in the negative range (n = 11) or intermediate range (n = 5) for participants without ADNC copathology. Four participants with ADNC had p-tau217 concentrations in the positive range; and 1, in the intermediate range.

Conclusions and relevance: Participants with high-stage CTE had higher concentrations of plasma eMTBR-tau than those with low-stage or no CTE; concentrations were highest among those with CTE and comorbid ADNC. Plasma eMTBR-tau may represent a feasible biomarker candidate for high-stage CTE tau tangle neuropathology. Larger autopsy and clinical validation studies are needed to establish overall diagnostic accuracy and specificity of plasma eMTBR-tau for CTE neuropathology, in addition to the associated prognostic and clinical implications.

item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: Ganfeborole and BTZ-043 are new drugs that may improve tuberculosis treatment.

Methods: In this phase 2, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned participants with rifampin-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis to receive the standard four-drug combination (isoniazid-rifampin-pyrazinamide-ethambutol; HRZE) for 24 weeks; bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin for 16 weeks; or one of 10 new four-drug combinations for 16 weeks. The new regimens contained ganfeborole, BTZ-043, or both, with combinations of bedaquiline, delamanid, moxifloxacin, pyrazinamide, pretomanid, and linezolid. The primary end point was the log10(time to positivity) slope (rate of change from baseline to week 12 in the time to Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a positive sputum culture). The treatment effect was assessed as the Bayesian posterior probability of superiority of each new regimen to HRZE with respect to the primary end point (results were used to select regimens for further evaluation, rather than for characterization of efficacy).

Results: A total of 401 participants underwent randomization; 371 were included in the modified intention-to-treat population and 400 in the safety population. We identified two promising regimens for further evaluation: ganfeborole-bedaquiline-pretomanid-moxifloxacin (BPMG) and BTZ-043-bedaquiline-delamanid-moxifloxacin (BDMT). The log10(time to positivity) slope was 0.129 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.112 to 0.146) with BPMG and 0.142 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.126 to 0.160) with BDMT, as compared with 0.118 log10(days) per week (95% Bayesian credible interval, 0.105 to 0.131) with HRZE, for a relative difference of 9.1% (95% Bayesian credible interval, -8.6 to 29.0) and 20.5% (95% Bayesian credible interval, 2.7 to 41.1), respectively, and a posterior probability of superiority of 0.83 and 0.99. The incidence of adverse events of grade 3 or higher was 38% in the BPMG group (none of the participants discontinued), 28% in the BDMT group (one discontinued because of a drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms), and 24% in the HRZE group (none discontinued). Bedaquiline-moxifloxacin-pyrazinamide-BTZ-043 was discontinued because of hepatotoxic effects.

Conclusions: In this trial, two four-drug regimens, one with ganfeborole and one with BTZ-043, showed evidence of potential efficacy and a safety profile that did not preclude progression to further evaluation. item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: What's Blood Got to Do with It? Identifying MPDS® Dispatch Codes Most Commonly Associated with Prehospital Blood Administration
item.description:
Objectives: This study aimed to identify Medical Priority Dispatch System (MPDS®) codes most frequently associated with prehospital blood utilization.

Methods: We examined Delaware's prehospital blood database to determine dispatch codes where low titer group O positive whole blood (LTOWB) was administered. We calculated the number of blood units under each dispatch code within the study period (May 2023- February 2026). Using this data, we identified the MPDS® codes associated with the highest number of blood units, including the top five codes overall, top medical codes, and as well as blood utilization rates for penetrating versus blunt traumas.

Results: The most frequent blood utilization came from the following dispatch codes: 29D02 (traffic collision, high mechanism) 32 patients, 27D04G (penetrating trauma with central wounds) 32 patients, 29D02M (auto versus pedestrian) 28 patients, 29D05 (traffic collision with entrapment) 24 patients, and 29D02L (auto versus bicycle/motorcycle) 20 patients. These five dispatch codes accounted for 29% of all prehospital LTOWB utilized within the 33-month study period. Analyzing blood utilization for non-traumatic dispatch codes revealed: 21D04/21D04M (dangerous hemorrhage, medical) 18 patients, 21D03/21D03M (hemorrhage, not alert, medical) 13 patients, 9E01/M9E01/M9E02 (cardiac or respiratory arrest/death, not breathing) 13 patients, and 21D05/21D05M (hemorrhage, abnormal breathing, medical) 7 patients. These four dispatch codes accounted for 11% (51 patients) of LTOWB utilization. When performing odds ratio analysis to determine odds of blood administration, we found 27D04G, 29D02M, and 29D02L to be statistically significant with 95% confidence intervals of [0.35- 0.87], [2.42- 5.72], [1.47- 3.91], and odds ratios of 0.55, 3.72, and 2.40, respectively. Additionally, our analysis demonstrated that patients with MPDS® coding for penetrating trauma with a delta level priority (27D) have higher likelihood of prehospital blood administration than delta priority high mechanism traffic incidents (29D). This comparison showed an OR of 10.40 that blood would be given to the penetrating trauma patient with a 95% confidence interval of [7.93- 13.66].

Conclusions: Specific MPDS® codes are strongly associated with prehospital blood utilization. Identifying these patterns offers a unique opportunity for emergency medical services systems to implement automatic blood dispatch protocols based on dispatch code.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Respiratory Syncytial Virus-Related Pediatric Intensive Care Unit Admissions in Children During Their Second RSV Season
item.description:
Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalization rates are highest among children younger than 2 years. For certain high-risk children entering their second RSV season, the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab is recommended. Little is known regarding preexisting health conditions as risk factors for RSV-related respiratory failure in children during their second RSV season.

Objective: To describe children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) for severe RSV by classifying them by their nirsevimab eligibility status and preexisting health conditions, and comparing their demographic and clinical characteristics.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study analyzed US children aged 8 to 23 months admitted to the PICU in 30 pediatric hospitals in the 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025 RSV seasons. All children had an RSV-positive result from a respiratory sample and received respiratory support with high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, or invasive mechanical ventilation. Analyses were based on the US criteria for second-season nirsevimab eligibility as recommended in August 2023.

Exposure: Preexisting health conditions potentially associated with increased risk of severe RSV disease. Patients were classified into 4 mutually exclusive groups of eligibility status and preexisting health conditions: (1) met nirsevimab eligibility criteria, (2) with other identified RSV risk conditions (with some evidence of increased risk for severe RSV), (3) with other preexisting conditions, and (4) with no preexisting conditions.

Main outcomes and measures: Patient demographic characteristics and level of respiratory support received were compared by level of preexisting health conditions.

Results: A total of 574 children (median [IQR] age, 1.2 [1.1-1.5] years; 317 males [55.2%]) were included. Overall, 47 patients (8.2%) met the nirsevimab eligibility criteria, 76 (13.2%) had other identified RSV risk conditions, 96 (16.7%) had other preexisting conditions, and 355 (61.8%) had no preexisting conditions. A higher proportion of children who met nirsevimab eligibility criteria required invasive mechanical ventilation vs children with other identified RSV risk conditions, those with other preexisting health conditions, or those with no preexisting health conditions (40.4% [19 of 47] vs 17.1% [13 of 76], 10.4% [10 of 96], 5.9% [21 of 355]; P for trend <.001).

Conclusions and relevance: Among children admitted to the PICU for severe RSV, 8.2% met the nirsevimab eligibility criteria and 13.2% had other identified RSV risk conditions. These findings might help inform future deliberations regarding second RSV season recommendations for nirsevimab eligibility in the US.

item.description:
Importance: The absence of milk fat globule membrane (MFGM) in infant formula may contribute to the differences between breastfed and formula-fed infants.

Objective: To test whether MFGM-enriched infant formula benefits cognitive development of exclusively formula-fed infants.

Design, setting, and participants: This clinician-blinded, researcher-blinded, and participant-blinded randomized clinical trial of exclusively formula-fed infants with a reference group (exclusively breastfed) included full-term singleton infants under 2 months of age, who were recruited from the community (May 2020 to April 2022). Follow-up was completed in June 2024 and analyses completed in September 2025.

Interventions: Randomized infants received either MFGM-enriched formula (treatment group: 0.55 g per 100.00 g of MFGM component phospholipid from MFGM Lipid 100 [New Zealand Milk Products, Fonterra Co-Operative Group Limited]) or standard formula (control group: no added MFGM, 0.29 g per 100.00 g of MFGM component phospholipid) from randomization to 12 months of age.

Main outcomes and measures: The Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, 4th Edition scales for cognitive, language, motor, emotional, and behavioral development, in which the mean (SD) score is 100 (15), with scores below 85 classified as delayed, were administered at ages 12 months and 24 months; the primary outcome was the 12-month cognitive score. Caregivers reported health, language, development, growth, safety, and tolerance.

Results: There were 416 randomized formula-fed infants (mean [SD] age, 36.6 [11.5] days; 209 males [50.2%]) and 204 reference group infants. Primary outcome data were available for 382 randomized infants (91.8%), including 193 (93.2%) of 207 in the treatment group and 189 (90.4%) of 209 in the control group. The mean (SD) 12-month cognitive scores in the treatment group (100.1 [11.9]) and control group (99.4 [14.1]) were not significant (adjusted mean difference, 0.68 [95% CI, -1.94 to 3.31]; P = .61). There was a significantly lower risk of delayed cognition (<85) at age 12 months in the treatment group compared with the control group (10.0 [4.8%] vs 24.1 [11.5%]; adjusted relative risk, 0.42 [95% CI, 0.20-0.90]; P = .03), and the mean (SD) language scores at age 24 months were higher in the treatment group compared with the control group (93.0 [16.3] vs 90.0 [16.6]; adjusted mean difference, 2.87 [95% CI, 0.10-5.65]; P = .04), although this difference was not statistically significant after controlling for caregiver educational level. Other secondary developmental outcomes, as well as growth and safety outcomes, were mostly not significant.

Conclusions and relevance: In this randomized clinical trial of MFGM-supplemented formula compared with standard formula among nonbreastfed infants, mean cognitive scores were not improved, although a reduction in the number of infants with cognitive delay is worthy of further investigation.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Metastatic Prostate Cancer Treatment Variation in Veterans
item.description:
Importance: Not all men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) receive the recommended combination therapy of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) and/or chemotherapy.

Objective: To determine factors associated with combination therapy use among veterans with mCSPC in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) system.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included US veterans diagnosed with mCSPC between January 1, 2023, through December 31, 2024, who were followed up through June 30, 2025. National multicenter data were obtained from the VHA electronic health record, community care settings (private care paid with VHA benefits), and Medicare. All included veterans were identified through a validated natural language processing algorithm, were followed up in the VHA for at least 2 years prior to their metastatic diagnosis, were provided ADT within the first 6 months of diagnosis, and received no prostate cancer-directed therapy in the year prior to diagnosis.

Exposure: Clinical factors (eg, comorbidities, frailty, prostate cancer burden at diagnosis) and nonclinical factors (eg, annual household income, neighborhood disadvantage) were investigated to determine their association with the outcome.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was receipt of combination therapy (ie, ADT plus ARPI [abiraterone, enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide] and/or docetaxel) vs ADT alone. Information on these treatments was obtained through pharmacy records. Multilevel logistic regression models were used and marginal predicted probabilities were reported to determine the associations of factors with receipt of combination therapy. Variation among VHA facilities was reported.

Results: A total of 4023 veterans (mean [SD] age, 75.3 [8.0] years) met eligibility criteria. Of these patients, 2339 (58.1%) had de novo metastatic disease, while 1684 (41.9%) had recurrent disease. Overall, 2564 patients (63.7%) received combination therapy. In adjusted analyses, older veterans (eg, aged 85-89 years: predicted probability, -14.1 [95% CI, -20.5 to -8.2] percentage points [pp]) and veterans with more comorbidities (eg, congestive heart failure: predicted probability, -7.5 [95% CI, -12.9 to -2.5] pp) were less likely to receive combination therapy. Annual household income and neighborhood disadvantage were not associated with receipt of combination therapy. Patients treated by urologists were less likely to receive combination therapy than patients treated by hematologist-oncologists (predicted probability, -23.7 [95% CI, -27.4 to -19.6] pp). Use of combination therapy ranged from 34% to 78% among VHA facilities.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of veterans with de novo and recurrent mCSPC, receipt of combination therapy was high; annual household income and neighborhood disadvantage had no association with treatment use. The study findings suggest that the region where a veteran lives, the facility where they receive care, and the type of cancer specialist they see are factors of the variation in combination therapy use that need further exploration.

Importance: Compression-only cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CO-CPR) has been widely promoted to encourage bystander intervention in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but long-term trends in bystander CPR and the associations between CPR type and outcomes in pediatric OHCA remain unclear.

Objective: To evaluate temporal trends in bystander CPR type and the associations with clinical outcomes among children with OHCA in Japan.

Design, setting, and participants: This cohort study included patients aged 17 years or younger with known receipt of bystander CPR documented in the nationwide All-Japan Utstein Registry from January 1, 2005, to December 31, 2023. Data analysis was performed from November 24, 2025, to September 2, 2026, including additional analyses conducted during the revision process.

Exposures: Bystander CPR was categorized as rescue-breathing CPR (RB-CPR), CO-CPR, or no bystander CPR.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was 30-day neurologically favorable survival rate; secondary outcomes were 30-day survival rate and prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Temporal trends were assessed with multinomial logistic regression, and associations between CPR type and outcomes were evaluated using modified Poisson regression with robust variance estimation, with CO-CPR serving as the reference.

Results: Among 26 785 pediatric patients with OHCA (median [IQR] age, 2.0 [0-12] years; 16 254 males [60.7%]), 6543 (24.4%) received RB-CPR, 9112 (34.0%) received CO-CPR, and 11 130 (41.6%) received no bystander CPR. The adjusted probability of CO-CPR increased from 14.6% (95% CI, 13.1%-16.1%) in 2005 to 55.1% (95% CI, 52.5%-57.6%) in 2023, whereas RB-CPR declined from 41.7% (95% CI, 39.7%-43.7%) to 10.4% (95% CI, 8.7%-12.1%). The adjusted probability of receiving no bystander CPR plateaued at approximately 35.0% after 2013. Neurologically favorable 30-day survival rate occurred in 3.6% receiving no bystander CPR, 9.5% receiving CO-CPR, and 16.0% receiving RB-CPR. Compared with CO-CPR, RB-CPR was associated with a higher 30-day neurologically favorable survival rate (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 1.71; 95% CI, 1.57-1.86), 30-day survival rate (ARR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.42-1.61), and prehospital ROSC (ARR, 1.62; 95% CI, 1.51-1.75), whereas receipt of no bystander CPR was associated with lower probabilities of these outcomes.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of children with OHCA, increasing CO-CPR use coincided with declining RB-CPR but not with further reductions in untreated arrests after 2013. No bystander CPR was associated with worse outcomes compared with CO-CPR and RB-CPR. RB-CPR had more favorable outcomes than CO-CPR, supporting the continued importance of rescue breathing in pediatric resuscitation.

item.description:
Objectives: Permanent onboard storage of red blood cells (RBC) units could facilitate timely prehospital transfusion but may expose blood products to cumulative transport-related mechanical stress. We evaluated the quality of RBC units stored continuously in operational ground ambulances under real-world emergency medical service conditions.

Methods: In this randomized controlled experimental study of RBC units, leukoreduced RBC units were randomly assigned to continuous onboard ambulance storage from day 7 to day 42 (n = 12) or standard blood bank storage at 2-6 °C for 42 days (n = 14). Samples were analyzed on days 7, 28, and 42. The primary outcome was hemolysis. Secondary outcomes included plasma biochemistry and storage-induced microerythrocytes (SMEs), an emerging morphological marker associated with post-transfusion RBC recovery. Temporal trajectories of SME levels were assessed using repeated-measures multivariate analysis of variance and fixed-effects panel models.

Results: All RBC units remained below the European regulatory hemolysis threshold of 0.8% at day 42. Hemolysis was higher in ambulance-stored units at day 28 (Hodges-Lehmann difference, +0.043 percentage points; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.010-0.076; p = 0.015) and day 42 (+0.096 percentage points; 95% CI, 0.029-0.176; p = 0.008). The SME levels increased in both groups, with a significant time-by-group interaction (p = 0.034) indicating different temporal trajectories. Additional SME accumulation in ambulance-stored units occurred predominantly between days 28 and 42. At day 42, the mean between-group SME difference was +9.04 percentage points (95% CI, -0.66 to 18.73; p = 0.066). The available sample was insufficient to exclude moderate or larger between-group differences. Biochemical changes were broadly similar between groups.

Conclusions: Continuous onboard RBC storage in operational ground ambulances maintained all units within regulatory hemolysis limits through day 42. However, higher hemolysis and late divergence in SME accumulation suggest that prolonged ambulance exposure may influence RBC storage quality. These findings provide preliminary support for the feasibility of continuous onboard RBC storage, particularly earlier in the storage period, but do not establish equivalence with conventional blood bank storage.

Importance: Ionizing radiation from medical imaging may increase brain tumor risk.

Objective: To quantify brain tumor risk associated with radiation exposure from medical imaging in children and adolescents.

Design, setting, and participants: Retrospective cohort study of children born from 1996 through 2016 who were enrolled from birth in 6 US health care systems or Ontario, Canada, and were alive and cancer-free at age 2 years, with follow-up through December 31, 2017 (US sites), and December 31, 2024 (Ontario).
