item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Prehospital Trauma Compendium: Prehospital Management of Pediatric Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Circulatory Arrest - A Joint Position Statement and Resource Document of NAEMSP, ACS-COT, ACEP, and AAP
item.description:
In 2014 the National Association of EMS Physicians (NAEMSP), American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma (ACS-COT), American College of Emergency Physicians (ACEP), and American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published the first joint position statement discussing withholding and discontinuing resuscitation attempts for pediatric traumatic out-of-hospital circulatory arrest (TOHCA). Since then, the body of literature addressing pediatric TOHCA has evolved and evidence has grown that demonstrates the nearly uniformly poor prognosis of children who suffer circulatory arrest in the prehospital setting as a result of trauma. To support emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians in their approach to these high-acuity, low-frequency, and challenging cases, this project aimed to update guidance regarding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts for pediatric traumatic circulatory arrest. NAEMSP, ACEP, ACS-COT, and AAP recommend:EMS resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA should:Prioritize prompt identification of patients who may benefit from transport to definitive care at trauma centers when safe and appropriate. On-scene resuscitation should be balanced against the potential benefit of transfer to a proximate trauma center.Emphasize the identification of reversible causes of traumatic circulatory arrest and timely use of clinically indicated life-saving interventions (LSIs) within the EMS clinician's scope of practice. These include:External hemorrhage control with direct pressure, wound packing, and tourniquetsAirway management using the least-invasive airway interventions required to achieve and maintain airway patency, oxygenation, and adequate ventilation.Chest decompression if clinical concern for tension pneumothorax. Empiric bilateral decompression is not recommended in the absence of suspected thoracic trauma.External chest compressions and ventilations have a larger role in pediatric TOHCA resuscitation than in adult TOHCA resuscitation, with children frequently having TOHCA secondary to head injury, hypoxia and other non-hemorrhagic mechanisms. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) should be provided when the cause of circulatory arrest is unclear.Epinephrine is of lower priority than other LSIs.Consider point of care ultrasound (POCUS) to guide decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation efforts.Resuscitation attempts may be withheld in pediatric TOHCA patients with:Injuries that are incompatible with life (e.g., decapitation, hemi-corpectomy, incineration).Evidence of prolonged circulatory arrest (e.g., rigor mortis, dependent lividity, decomposition).Advanced care planning documents that indicate Do Not Resuscitate (DNR)/ Do Not Attempt Resuscitation (DNAR)/Allow Natural Death medical orders.Resuscitation attempts may be discontinued in pediatric TOHCA patients who:Have no return of spontaneous circulation after provision of at least 15 minutes of high-quality CPR in addition to performance of other lifesaving interventions directed at treating potentially reversible causes of pediatric TOHCA. Longer durations of CPR, up to 30 minutes, may be considered for patients with positive predictors of survival such as organized rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander CPR, or with proximate access to a trauma center.Have known predictors of very low probability of survival such as penetrating trauma without proximate access to a trauma center, asystole, unwitnessed arrest, or lack of bystander CPR.Protocols guiding decisions to withhold or discontinue resuscitation of pediatric TOHCA benefit from oversight by EMS physicians in collaboration with pediatric experts and local or regional trauma system stakeholders. Implementation of such protocols for pediatric patients benefits from involvement of community stakeholders including family representatives, law enforcement, medical examiner, and child fatality review committees.Considerations for protocol implementation include local resource availability, EMS clinician and public safety, psychosocial support to surviving family members and emergency responders, and dignified handling of the deceased patient.Training needs for EMS clinicians include techniques to communicate with family members regarding the death of a child and understanding the clinician's own response to this low-frequency, high-emotion experience.

item.title: Crit Care Med: Prevalence and Characteristics of Coma in Latin American Critical Care Units: The COMA LATAM Study
item.description:
Objectives: To determine the point prevalence of coma across Latin American critical care units, characterize its etiology, and explore short-term outcomes.

Design: Multinational, cross-sectional point prevalence study with exploratory 14-day follow-up assessment.

Setting: Three hundred ninety-two hospitals across 19 Latin American countries, including ICUs, intermediate care units, neurocritical care units, cardiovascular ICUs, and trauma ICUs.

Patients: Adult patients (≥ 18 yr) meeting the Coma Epidemiology, Evaluation, and Therapy care survey (COME-TOGETHER) criteria on May 28, 2024. Patients under deep sedation or pharmacological coma induction were excluded unless the coma state preceded pharmacological intervention.

Interventions: None (observational study).

Measurements and main results: Among 8305 critically ill patients, 1145 met coma criteria (point prevalence 13.8%), with country-specific rates ranging from 5.1% to 36.8%. Individual patient data were available for 729 patients (63.7%). Traumatic brain injury was the leading individual cause (24.8%), followed by hypoxic-anoxic brain injury (14.6%) and intracerebral hemorrhage (13.5%). When categorized by pathophysiology, vascular causes predominated (48.6%), followed by traumatic brain injury (24.8%) and other causes (26.6%). Age-stratified analysis revealed trauma predominantly affecting younger patients, while cerebrovascular causes predominated in older groups. Among patients with 14-day follow-up data (29% of cohort), mortality was 29.2%, with 67.7% of survivors recovering from coma. Only the Charlson Comorbidity Index was independently associated with implementation of life-sustaining therapy limitations (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22; 95% CI, 1.15-1.30; p < 0.001).

Conclusions: Coma affects nearly one in seven ICU beds across Latin America, with substantial country variation and distinct age-dependent etiology patterns. The significant burden highlights the need for targeted prevention strategies and specialized neurocritical care resources throughout the region.

item.title: Am J Respir Crit Care Med: Charcot-Leyden crystals drive a localized inflammatory niche around mucus plugs in Allergic Bronchopulmonary Aspergillosis
item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
Rationale: Mucus plugging causes airflow obstruction, morbidity, and mortality in chronic respiratory diseases. Charcot-Leyden crystals (CLCs), formed from eosinophil-derived Galectin-10, are frequently observed in pathologic mucus, but their role in disease is unclear.

Objectives: To define the prevalence, inflammatory context, and functional role of CLCs in mucus plugs, using acute allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) as a model of eosinophilic muco-obstructive disease.

Methods: Airway samples from 19 patients with acute ABPA and 61 disease controls were analyzed for CLCs and Galectin-10. Paired samples from plugged and unplugged bronchial mucosal biopsies defined the spatial relationship between CLCs and inflammation. A novel mouse model demonstrated the contribution of CLCs to airway obstruction and inflammation and enabled evaluation of CLC-directed imaging and therapy.

Measurements and main results: Airway CLCs were a sensitive and specific marker of acute ABPA. CLC-containing mucus plugs were surrounded by a localized type 2 inflammatory niche, alongside eosinophils, neutrophils and extracellular traps, whereas inflammation was minimal in unplugged airways from the same patients, or plugs lacking CLCs. In mice, CLC-containing plugs induced persistent airway obstruction and local inflammation, both reduced by a crystal-dissolving anti-Galectin-10 antibody. Galectin-10 concentrations provided a quantitative biomarker of acute ABPA, while a CLC-targeted positron emission tomography tracer enabled noninvasive visualization of crystal-rich plugs.

Conclusions: CLC-containing mucus plugs form focal inflammatory niches in acute ABPA, and experimental CLC deposition is sufficient to promote persistent airway obstruction and inflammation. These findings identify CLCs as a biomarker, imaging target, and tractable therapeutic target in eosinophilic muco-obstructive airway disease.

item.title: Crit Care: CT-based radiomics for interpretable outcome prediction after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a multicenter cohort study
item.description:
Background: Prognostic assessment after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) mainly relies on clinical variables and computed tomography (CT) findings, but current models often lack biological interpretability. We developed and validated a clinical-radiomics prognostic model and subsequently performed exploratory cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) proteomic characterization of model-defined risk phenotypes.

Methods: This multicenter cohort from the PROSAH-MPC registry included 879 patients across four hospitals. Patients from the primary center were split into training (n = 637) and internal validation (n = 160) cohorts, while patients from three other centers formed an external validation cohort (n = 82). Admission CT hemorrhagic lesions were automatically segmented using the validated BrainHemoAI platform, and radiomic features were extracted with PyRadiomics. Clinical, radiomics, and combined clinical-radiomics XGBoost models were developed and interpreted using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Risk scores from the clinical-radiomics model were applied to an independent prospective enrichment, gene setCSF​ proteomic cohort to define combined model-based high- and low-risk groups. Gene Ontology (GO)/ Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were performed.

Results: The combined model yielded AUCs of 0.892 and 0.820 in the internal test and external validation cohorts, respectively. Risk reclassification analyses suggested that radiomic features may provide complementary prognostic information. SHAP identified radiomic heterogeneity and key clinical variables as major predictors. Meanwhile, exploratory CSF proteomic analysis identified candidate differentially expressed proteins and associated pathway signals that differed between groups defined by high and low combined clinical-radiomics risk scores.

Conclusions: This clinical-radiomics prognostic model enables accurate outcome prediction and provides exploratory biological insight into unfavorable recovery after aSAH, supporting refined risk stratification and potential targeted therapeutic development.

item.title: Crit Care: Effect of megadose vitamin C in patients with sepsis: the CEMVIS randomized clinical trial
item.description:
Background: Previous randomized trials of vitamin C in sepsis have reported conflicting findings, but whether the effect of vitamin C varies according to septic shock status remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effect of megadose vitamin C in sepsis and explore whether treatment effect differed according to septic shock status.

Methods: CEMVIS was a multicenter, randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial conducted in four tertiary hospitals in China. Adults meeting Sepsis-3 criteria were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive intravenous vitamin C (12 g every 12 h for 4 days) or placebo using stratified randomization according to septic shock status. Patients were analyzed according to the modified intention-to-treat principle. The primary outcome was 28-day mortality.

Results: Between Feb 8, 2022, and Dec 25, 2024, 114 patients in the vitamin C group and 117 in the placebo group were included in the modified intention-to-treat population. 28-day mortality did not differ significantly between groups (35/114 [30.7%] vs 36/116 [31.0%]; odds ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.56-1.74; p = 0.97). No significant differences were observed in the duration of mechanical ventilation, vasopressor therapy, and renal replacement therapy, or in changes in SOFA scores over 96 hours. Prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant interaction according to septic shock status (P for interaction = 0.026), with the treatment effects on 28-day mortality numerically favoring vitamin C among patients without septic shock (15.4% vs 34%) and numerically favoring placebo among those with septic shock (38.7% vs 29%). Hypernatremia occurred more frequently in the vitamin C group (40/114 [35.1%] vs 24/117 [20.5%]; p = 0.02). Exploratory restricted cubic spline analyses showed that increasing lactate levels were associated with a progressive shift in treatment effect from potential benefit toward potential harm. Post hoc Bayesian analyses further provided probabilistic characterization of the potential treatment effect according to septic shock status.

Conclusions: The results of this trial do not support the routine use of megadose vitamin C to reduce 28-day mortality in patients with sepsis. Treatment effects may vary according to septic shock status.

item.title: Chest: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk prediction in individuals with and without impaired spirometry
item.description:
Background: Cardiovascular disease risk scores likely underestimate risk in individuals with impaired spirometry (airflow obstruction and preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm)).

Research question: How do risk scores perform between individuals with impaired and normal spirometry, and can they be improved by adding spirometry and dyspnea?

Study design and methods: Ten-year incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) ie., myocardial infarction, stroke or death from coronary heart disease, from 7 US population-based cohorts was used for this analysis. The pooled cohorts' equations' (PCE) ability to predict MACE was compared between normal and impaired spirometry. Cox-models adding spirometry, dyspnea to PCE variables were evaluated for improvement in MACE prediction.

Results: Among 26523 participants, those with impaired (N=7547) compared with normal (N=18932) spirometry had a higher incidence of MACE (14% vs 7%), hazard ratio 95%CI 1.25[1.17,1.34] adjusted for PCE variables. Discrimination using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)95%CI of the PCE for MACE was 0.792[0.780,0.803] vs 0.740[0.724,0.755] in normal vs impaired spirometry. Discrimination of MACE improved slightly by adding to the PCE: dyspnea plus 1)impaired spirometry 0.792[0.783,0.800], 2)PRISm, mild, moderate+ airflow obstruction 0.792[0.783,0.801], 3)FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC splines 0.793[0.784,0.802], compared with PCE variables 0.790[0.781,0.798]. The differences in AUC[95%CI] were: 1)0.002[0.001,0.003]p=0.002, 2)0.002[0.001,0.004]p=0.002, 3)0.003[0.002,0.005]p=0.0005 respectively. Among participants with impaired spirometry, only the model that added FEV1%predicted, FEV1/FVC continuous and dyspnea to the PCE showed improvement in AUC[95%CI], 0.750[0.735,0.765] vs 0.746[0.730,0.761] for PCE variables, difference of 0.004[0.001,0.008]p=0.008. item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Towards a national drug checking database to monitor the drug supply and prevent drug-related harms: A narrative review
item.description:
Objectives: The changing drug supply poses challenges for preventing drug-related harms. Timely drug supply information is critical for public health and clinical responses, yet existing surveillance systems lack the nuance and speed to detect emerging trends. Drug checking services may help address these gaps by enhancing monitoring of drug supplies, informing public health and clinical interventions, and supporting evidence-based policymaking. This review examines the evolution of drug checking in the United States, evaluates the strengths and limitations of these data relative to existing surveillance systems, and provides recommendations for integrating drug checking into national drug surveillance efforts.

Methods: We conducted a narrative review to synthesize the current evidence on drug checking with an emphasis on the U.S.

Context: Findings from published studies were supplemented by the expertise of subject matter experts actively engaged in drug checking research, practice, and policy.

Results: Compared to traditional drug surveillance, drug checking data offer several advantages, including face validity (representing drugs at the level of consumption rather than from upstream seizures), timeliness (days to weeks rather than months to years), breadth (inclusion of novel psychoactive substances) and depth (inclusion of contextual cues). Four recommendations emerged from the review: expanding sustainable funding; advancing drug checking technologies; strengthening legal protections for programs and clients; and establishing data governance and stewardship frameworks to support data sharing, quality, and privacy.

Conclusions: Greater investment in drug checking services, supported by coordinated data systems and enabling policies, could strengthen surveillance and advance efforts to prevent and reduce drug-related harms.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: Higher county-level need is associated with greater naloxone distribution from U.S. syringe services programs in 2023: A cross-sectional study
item.description:
Objectives: To assess whether U.S. syringe services programs (SSPs) in counties with higher levels of need in 2022 had greater financial resources and larger-scale delivery of overdose prevention interventions in 2023.

Methods: This study utilized a cross-sectional design. As a measure of underlying, community-level need, our primary exposure was 2022 county-level opioid overdose fatalities, categorized as low (1-33), moderate (34-198), or high (199-1923). Outcomes included annual SSP budget, number of naloxone recipients from the SSP, naloxone doses distributed by the SSP, and buprenorphine availability at the SSP. Using weighted generalized estimating equations with exchangeable correlation structures to account for clustering of SSPs within Census divisions, we used gamma, negative binomial, and logit specifications as appropriate for each outcome.

Results: SSPs reported a median budget of $141,842; 596 naloxone recipients; 2001 naloxone doses distributed; and 44% had integrated buprenorphine. Compared to SSPs in low overdose fatality counties, SSPs in moderate- and high overdose fatality counties had significantly larger budgets, greater number of naloxone recipients and greater number of naloxone doses distributed. SSPs in higher need counties were not significantly more likely to have buprenorphine available (aOR=1.40; 95% CI:0.72-2.75; p = 0.321).

Conclusion: Our findings showed that higher levels of need were positively associated with greater financial resources for and naloxone distribution from SSPs in 2023 but was not associated with greater buprenorphine availability. Effects were nonsignificant in time-lagged models, however.

item.description:
Purpose: We examined whether early co-administration of landiolol and adrenaline improves successful extubation, hemodynamics, and 48-h outcomes in a swine ventricular fibrillation (VF) model.

Methods: In this prospective, randomized, investigator-blinded study, VF was electrically induced in healthy piglets and left untreated for 8 min. Thirty-nine female Landrace/Large White piglets were randomized (1:1:1): adrenaline 0.02 mg/kg plus saline, adrenaline plus esmolol 0.5 mg/kg, or adrenaline plus landiolol 0.02 mg/kg. Treatment was administered at the initiation of mechanical cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), 2 min before attempting defibrillation. Primary outcome was successful extubation. Secondary outcomes included return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), 48-h survival, 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery, and hemodynamic variables during and after CPR.

Results: Successful extubation occurred in 2/13 (15%) control, 6/13 (46%) esmolol, and 9/13 (69%) landiolol animals (overall p = 0.021); the rate was significantly higher with landiolol than with control (adjusted p = 0.046). The landiolol group had higher observed rates of ROSC and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery than the control group; these secondary analyses were exploratory. No pairwise difference was significant for 48-h survival. Exploratory analyses during the first 4 min of CPR identified higher observed values for selected hemodynamic variables and end-tidal carbon dioxide in the landiolol group at specific time points. Esmolol had intermediate observed outcome rates.

Conclusions: Early administration of landiolol with adrenaline was associated with a higher successful extubation rate and better observed early CPR hemodynamics compared with adrenaline alone and had the highest rates of ROSC, 48-h survival, and 48-h survival with complete neurological recovery. item.description:
Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a common cause of acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in patients with pneumonia, sepsis, aspiration of gastric contents, severe trauma, or other inciting triggers. Critical components of management include identification and treatment of the underlying cause of ARDS as well as avoidance of ventilator-induced lung injury and volume overload. Ongoing areas of controversy include the best strategy for supporting nonintubated patients, personalization of positive end-expiratory pressure, the role of innovative ventilatory strategies, and the use of glucocorticoids. item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Commercial Health Care Prices and Medical Debt in the US
item.description:
Importance: Medical debt remains a major source of financial strain for US households. Although commercial health care prices vary substantially across markets, little is known about how these prices are associated with medical debt.

Objective: To examine the association between changes in commercial to Medicare price ratios and changes in medical debt in collections across US local markets.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study used data from multiple geographic areas (referred to hereinafter as geozips) in the US. Commercial to Medicare price ratio data were obtained from FAIR Health claims for 2020 and 2022 to 2023, and medical debt outcomes were measured using the Urban Institute Credit Panel in August 2020 and August 2023. Analyses were conducted between October 2025 and August 2026 at the geozip level using a 2-period ecologic first-difference model.

Exposures: Changes in commercial to Medicare price ratios for professional, outpatient, and inpatient services.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the change in the share of adults with with medical debt in collections exceeding $500.

Results: The sample included 479 geozips in the US. A 1-unit increase in the professional commercial to Medicare price ratio was associated with a 4.3-percentage point increase (0.043; 95% CI, 0.027-0.060; P < .001) in the share of adults with medical debt in collections above $500. Changes in the inpatient and outpatient price ratios were not statistically associated with medical debt in collections exceeding $500.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of US geozips from 2020 to 2023, increases in commercial to Medicare price ratios for professional services were associated with increases in medical debt in collections, whereas changes in inpatient and outpatient price ratios were not. These findings suggest that commercial price increases in services more directly tied to patient cost sharing coincide with increased financial hardship.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Prevalence of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy Without Contact Sport Repetitive Head Impact Exposure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
item.description:
Importance: A pooled baseline prevalence of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in populations without repetitive head impact (RHI) exposure is needed to contextualize prevalence in other cohorts.

Objective: To estimate the pooled prevalence of CTE in populations without documented contact sport-based RHI exposure.

Data sources: PubMed and Embase were searched from inception through February 23, 2026, using terms for CTE, prevalence, epidemiology, and neuropathology.

Study selection: Studies reporting CTE prevalence in cohorts without documented contact sport RHI history were included and classified by ascertainment rigor into a primary group with verified absence of contact sport RHI or a secondary unscreened reference cohort. Studies were excluded for cohort overlap or for RHI-linked comorbid conditions (eg, epilepsy).

Data extraction and synthesis: Data were independently extracted by 2 authors, with discrepancy resolved by a third. Risk of bias and quality were assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute checklist. Pooled prevalence was calculated using a random-effects model with restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity (I2 and τ2) and robustness (leave-one-out sensitivity analysis) were assessed.

Main outcomes and measures: Confirmed CTE in individuals without documented contact sport RHI history was estimated using pooled prevalence and 95% CIs.

Results: Twelve cohort studies (4421 individuals; weighted mean age at death, 75.1 years; 2481 male [56.1%]) were identified. In the primary analysis of 7 cohorts with verified absence of contact sport RHI (1604 individuals), 12 cases of CTE were identified (crude prevalence, 0.75% [95% CI, 0.43%-1.30%]); pooled prevalence was 1.06% (95% CI, 0.10%-10.79%), reflecting substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 87.0%) and limited precision from few cases and presence of an outlier with 5 of 7 individuals with CTE. Excluding the outlier yielded a pooled prevalence of 0.70% (95% CI, 0.28%-1.74%) and reduced heterogeneity (I2 = 6.6%). In the 5 unscreened reference cohorts (2817 individuals), 17 cases of CTE were identified (crude prevalence, 0.60% [95% CI, 0.38%-0.96%]). Across all 12 cohorts, the crude prevalence was 0.66% (95% CI, 0.46%-0.94%), and the pooled prevalence was 0.85% (95% CI, 0.24%-2.89%).

Conclusions and relevance: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 cohort studies not selected for contact sport-based RHI exposure found that CTE pathology was rare, with a baseline prevalence of approximately 1%. These findings provide a reference point for interpreting CTE prevalence in other populations, including cohorts with contact sport exposure.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Firearm Homicide Surges From 1979 to 2023
item.description:
Importance: US firearm homicide rates surged twice in the past 35 years. Better understanding of such surges could aid prevention.

Objective: To compare the demographic and geographic distribution of surge deaths and examine state-level correlates of surge severity across the 1985-1993 and 2014-2021 firearm homicide surge periods.

Design, setting, and participants: This serial cross-sectional study obtained homicide counts from 1979 to 2023, stratified by race, sex, age group, county urbanicity, and state, from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The firearm homicide surge periods 1985 to 1993 and 2014 to 2021 were analyzed. Although both Black and Hispanic people in the US bear a disproportionate burden of firearm homicide, Hispanic ethnicity was not consistently coded in mortality records over the study period (1979-2023); thus, a single categorization of Black or other race was used. Data analyses were conducted in April 2025 to September 2026.

Exposure: Presurge levels and presurge-to-surge changes in state measures of drug-market violence, proxy measures for firearm availability and use, economic strength, social or economic disadvantage, urban concentration, social or economic disruption, and policing capacity.

Main outcomes and measures: Annualized firearm homicide surge rates (deaths per 100 000 population, above presurge rates). Correlations between state-level surge rates and proxy measures were calculated.

Results: The 2014-2021 surge produced an estimated mean (SE) of 31 489 (509) firearm surge deaths, with a mean (SE) annualized rate of 1.20 (0.02) deaths per 100 000 population per year above presurge rates. In the 1985-1993 surge, the mean (SE) number of firearm surge deaths was 24 276 (580), with a mean (SE) annualized rate of 1.09 (0.03) deaths per 100 000 population. Both surges were driven entirely by firearm homicide, as non-firearm homicides declined over both periods. Deaths of young urban Black males (aged 15-24 years) accounted for 47% of 1985-1993 surge deaths but only 14% of the 2014-2021 surge. Compared with the 1985-1993 surge, during the 2014-2021 surge, the mean (SE) firearm homicide surge rates increased for females (0.15 [0.02] vs 0.38 [0.01]), people of races other than Black (0.22 [0.02] vs 0.48 [0.01]), and rural residents (0.13 [0.04] vs 0.83 [0.03]). Across US states, the 1985-1993 surge correlated with crack cocaine market activity (r = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.19-0.64), while the 2014-2021 surge correlated with presurge firearm availability proxies (r = 0.68 [95% CI, 0.50-0.81] for value of stolen firearms per capita) and COVID-19-related death rates (r = 0.61; 95% CI, 0.40-0.76). Across both eras, higher state-level surge rates correlated with social or economic disadvantage, including premature mortality, poverty rates, lower employment, and household instability.

Conclusions and relevance: In this serial cross-sectional study of US firearm homicide mortality, both the 2014-2021 surge, which was substantially larger and more demographically and geographically dispersed, and the 1985-1993 surge were associated with distinct proximal correlates but disproportionately affected states with broader structural vulnerabilities. Proximal drivers of rapid increases in homicide rates may exacerbate long-standing population vulnerabilities.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Multicomponent Lifestyle Intervention and Brain Aging: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Multicomponent lifestyle interventions show promise for promoting cognitive health, but their effects on clinically established brain aging markers among individuals with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) are unclear. Intervention adherence may influence intervention efficacy.

Objectives: To evaluate the association of combined aerobic exercise and cognitive training (ACT) with brain aging markers and to explore the role of intervention adherence.

Design, setting, and participants: This secondary analysis of a phase 2, single-blind, 2 × 2 factorial randomized clinical trial with data collection lasting up to 18 months per participant was conducted at 3 academic research facilities between April 1, 2018, and July 17, 2024. Among 911 individuals screened, 146 participants with aMCI were randomized. Data were analyzed from October 10, 2025, to January 8, 2026.

Interventions: The ACT intervention was compared with 3 other intervention arms during a 6-month period, including speed-of-processing training (SOP), cycling, and mental leisure activities plus stretching (MS).

Main outcomes and measures: Alzheimer disease signature for cortical thickness (ADSCT) and natural log-transformed white matter hyperintensity (ln-WMH) were assessed at baseline, post intervention, and at the 12- and 18-month follow-ups. Outcome-specific modified intention-to-treat analyses used 100 forward-only multiple imputations and age-, sex-, and site-adjusted linear mixed-effects models with a participant random intercept. Visit-specific complete-case and attendance analyses used participants observed at baseline and the relevant follow-up.

Results: Among 146 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 73.8 [5.7] years), 75 (51.4%) were male. A total of 144 participants had baseline ADSCT and 141 had baseline ln-WMH measurements. In primary analyses, compared with ACT, SOP was associated with greater worsening in 18-month ADSCT change (B = -0.060 [95% CI, -0.117 to -0.004] mm; P = .04), and MS was associated with greater 12-month worsening (B = -0.066 [95% CI, -0.122 to -0.011] mm; P = .02). No primary ln-WMH contrast was significant. In visit-specific complete cases, cycling was associated with greater 18-month ln-WMH progression than ACT (B = 0.452 [95% CI, 0.131-0.772] natural log units; P = .006). Exploratory within-ACT analyses linked each of 10 additional sessions to greater postintervention ADSCT change (B = 0.022 [95% CI, 0.002-0.042] mm; P = .03), but not ln-WMH change.

Conclusions and relevance: In this secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial of older adults with aMCI, ACT was associated with more favorable ADSCT change than SOP at 18 months and MS at 12 months. No primary ln-WMH contrast was significant. Attendance findings were post randomization and exploratory. Larger confirmatory trials are needed to verify these findings.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03313895.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Sleep-Wake Cycle Profiles and Incident Dementia and Cognitive Decline in Older Adults
item.description:
Importance: Sleep-wake cycle (SWC) disruptions are common in patients with dementia and potentially also in the preclinical phase of the disease. Accelerometers allow objective measures of multiple SWC dimensions: rest-activity rhythm (RAR), daytime activity, sleep, and chronotype, but these dimensions are rarely examined together.

Objective: This study examined the association of SWC profiles, incorporating the 4 SWC dimensions, with incident dementia and cognitive decline.

Design, setting, and participants: Prospective, UK population-based cohort study based on accelerometer data from the 2012 to 2013 wave of the Whitehall II cohort study, with a median (IQR) follow-up of 12.3 (12.0-12.7) years. Statistical analyses were conducted from June 2025 to March 2026. Participants were dementia-free aged 60 years or older with valid accelerometer data and covariates at baseline.

Exposure: Nine SWC profiles derived from 36 SWC metrics.

Main outcomes and measures: Incident dementia cases until March 2025 were retrieved from electronic health records. Cognitive tests were administered in 2012 to 2013, 2015 to 2016, and 2019 to 2022 and each test score was standardized based on 2012 to 2013 data and all tests averaged to derive a global cognitive z score.

Results: Among 3973 participants (median [IQR] age = 68.4 [64.7 to 74.0] years; 26% women), 379 dementia cases were recorded during a median 12.3-year follow-up. Compared with participants with robust RAR (high level and amplitude, stable, not fragmented), light-intensity physical activity (PA) and good sleep (profile 3), those with poorer RAR (low level and amplitude, unstable, fragmented) along with low PA and poor sleep (profile 7), or with high level and low amplitude RAR and restless sleep (profile 8) had higher dementia risk (hazard ratio, 1.94 [95% CI, 1.32 to 2.84], and 1.96 [95% CI, 1.27 to 3.03], respectively). In analyses on cognitive decline (3806 participants), profile 7 as well as the most sedentary profile with the poorest RAR (profile 9) had faster 10-year cognitive decline (-0.14 [95% CI, -0.26 to -0.02]) and -0.28 [95% CI, -0.44 to -0.13], respectively). Cognitive outcomes in participants with robust RAR and higher PA were similar, irrespective of sleep.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 3973 older adults, consideration of all SWC dimensions was important in identifying profiles associated with cognitive outcomes; further studies are needed to evaluate whether SWC interventions reduce the risk or delay onset of dementia.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Cost-Effectiveness of Alcohol Use Disorder Treatment for Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease
item.description:
Importance: Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of liver-related mortality and liver transplant. Combined behavioral interventions (CBI) and medications for alcohol use disorder (MAUD) are underutilized. Thus, it is critical to identify optimal therapeutic and cost-effective windows for CBI and MAUD in patients with ALD at earlier fibrosis stages.

Objective: To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of naltrexone and CBI in preventing cirrhosis in patients with ALD compared with no treatment.

Design, setting, and participants: This economic evaluation used a Markov state-transition model simulating lifetime disease progression and health care costs associated with ALD. The simulated patient cohort began at 45 years of age with active AUD and stage 3 fibrosis (F3) and could experience progression to compensated or decompensated cirrhosis.

Exposure: All patients were assumed to complete a 16-week course of naltrexone along with 52 weeks of CBI.

Main outcomes and measures: Primary outcomes included total health care cost, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. Secondary outcomes included liver-related mortality and progression to compensated and decompensated cirrhosis. Scenario and sensitivity analyses were performed to determine outcomes at earlier stages and with varied cost and model parameters.

Results: Without intervention, 61% of the cohort died from liver-related causes, 88% developed compensated cirrhosis, and 66% of those experienced progression to decompensated cirrhosis, with a lifetime cost of $79 799 per person. With treatment initiated at F3, liver-related mortality was reduced to 58%, lifetime compensated cirrhosis to 87%, and lifetime progression to decompensated cirrhosis to 62%, with a lifetime cost of $78 673. The treatment strategy dominated because the lifetime costs were lower and more QALYs were gained when compared with untreated natural history. Treatment was preferred in sensitivity analyses at relapse rates to 100% and adherence greater than 0%, in scenario analyses when treatment was initiated at stages F2 and F1, and for the models including societal and AUD costs.

Conclusions and relevance: In this economic evaluation of AUD treatment for patients with ALD, treating patients with ALD with naltrexone and CBI at F3 saved cost and was more effective than no treatment, reducing progression to compensated and decompensated cirrhosis. The results remained true at stages F1 and F2 fibrosis and when considering the societal costs and the costs of AUD. Future studies should include prospective evaluations of screening strategies combined with early treatment, as many patients are diagnosed at advanced stages of ALD.

item.title: Crit Care Med: ICU Mortality Associated With Clinically Important Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding: A Multistate Analysis
item.description:
Objectives: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding may increase mortality and time to discharge from the ICU. Conventional analyses ignore timing and treat bleeding as a binary event. We evaluated the association between time-dependent clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding and ICU mortality.

Design and setting: A multicenter cohort study using data from an international stress ulcer prophylaxis trial.

Patients: A total of 4821 invasively ventilated adult participants.

Interventions: None.

Measurements and main results: A multistate model was specified with two transient ICU states (bleed-free and post-bleed) and four absorbing states (ICU discharge or death, each with or without bleeding). The Aalen-Johansen method was used to estimate transition and state occupancy probabilities and to describe risks of different clinical courses. Follow-up was censored at 90 days. We fit two Cox models for time to death in the ICU regressing on time-dependent bleeding history while adjusting for age, sex, baseline Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score, admission category (medical/surgical/trauma), vasopressor/inotrope use and renal replacement therapy on study day 1 and randomized allocation of pantoprazole or placebo; a second model also adjusted for time-dependent covariates of advanced life support (invasive mechanical ventilation, vasopressor/inotrope use, and renal replacement therapy). Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding developed in 104 patients (2.2%) in the ICU. Median ICU length of stay for those who experienced bleeding was 19 days (interquartile range [IQR], 11-30 d) vs. 9 days (IQR, 5-15 d) for those who did not. Accounting for immortal time bias, the time-dependent indicator of clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding was associated with increased ICU mortality (hazard ratio, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.13-2.15). At any time, patients who experienced bleeding had approximately 1.6 times the hazard of ICU mortality compared with those without a history of bleeding.

Conclusions: Clinically important upper gastrointestinal bleeding as a time-dependent event is associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality.

item.title: Crit Care Med: Age-Related Differences in the Organ Donation Process Among Pediatric Brain-Dead Donors: A Nationwide Study in Japan
item.description:
Objectives: To characterize the pediatric organ donation process and age-related differences among brain-dead donors in Japan and evaluate organ-specific transplantation rates and graft survival across age groups.

Design: Nationwide retrospective cohort study.

Setting: National donor records maintained by the Japan Organ Transplant Network.

Patients: All pediatric (≤ 17 yr old) brain-dead organ donors in Japan between July 17, 2010, and March 31, 2024.

Interventions: None.

Measurement and main results: A total of 100 pediatric brain-dead organ donors were included. Donors were categorized into three age groups: younger than 6 years (n = 32), 6-14 years (n = 48), and 15-17 years (n = 20). The time intervals from hospital admission to organ procurement showed marked age-dependent prolongation, with median durations of 28, 19.5, and 13.5 days, respectively (p < 0.01). Younger donors were more frequently managed in children's hospitals and pediatric departments, whereas older donors were increasingly managed in emergency and critical care settings. Organ transplantation was achieved in 99% of donors. Organ-specific transplantation rates were consistently high for the heart, liver, and kidneys across all age groups, whereas lung and pancreas transplantation rates increased with donor age. During donor management, respiratory, cardiovascular, renal, and hepatic function were generally maintained or improved until procurement. No significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed for any organ type.

Conclusions: The pediatric organ donation process in Japan was substantially prolonged in an age-dependent manner, particularly among donors younger than 6 years. Despite prolonged donor management, transplantation rates remained high, and no significant age-related differences in graft survival were observed. These findings highlight the importance of sustained multidisciplinary and family support throughout the donation process and may provide insights for pediatric donation systems in low-volume settings.

item.title: Crit Care Med: High-Flow Nasal Cannula Versus Conventional Oxygen Therapy in Adults With De Novo Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis With Trial Sequential Analysis
item.description:
Objectives: To evaluate the efficacy of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) compared with conventional oxygen therapy (COT) in adults with de novo acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF) using a meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA).

Data sources: MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception to April 7, 2026.

Study selection: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing HFNC with COT in adults with de novo AHRF.

Data extraction: Two investigators independently performed study selection, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, and certainty assessment, with discrepancies resolved through discussion.

Data synthesis: A total of 13 RCTs involving 4294 patients were included in the analysis. Compared with COT, HFNC was associated with a lower risk of intubation (Risk ratio [RR], 0.88; 95% CI, 0.78-0.99; low certainty), but not mortality (RR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.83-1.10; moderate certainty). TSA indicated that the cumulative evidence was insufficient to establish a conclusive effect for either outcome. Although HFNC was associated with a statistically significant reduction in hospital length of stay (mean difference, -0.84 d; 95% CI, -1.26 to -0.43; low certainty), the clinical importance of this reduction remains uncertain. No significant differences were observed in escalation of therapy (RR, 0.87; 95% CI, 0.75-1.01; very low certainty), ICU admission (RR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.50-1.39; very low certainty), or ICU length of stay (mean difference, -0.10 d; 95% CI, -0.82 to 0.61; very low certainty).

Conclusions: In adults with de novo AHRF, HFNC may reduce the need for endotracheal intubation but probably does not improve survival compared with COT.

item.title: Crit Care Med: The Radiographic Lung Edema Score in Pediatric Acute Respiratory Failure: Associations With Systemic Inflammatory Biomarkers and Multiple Organ Dysfunction
item.description:
Objectives: Although chest radiographs (CXR) are among the most used imaging modalities in critically ill patients, their interpretation and clinical significance remain incompletely leveraged. The Radiographic Lung Edema (RALE) score is a prognostic bedside tool widely applied in adults to quantify lung edema on CXR. However, this score has been infrequently studied in children, and its potential to reflect broader aspects of critical illness pathophysiology beyond the lungs is unknown. We sought to determine the reproducibility of the RALE score, and whether higher RALE scores were associated with circulating inflammatory and endothelial biomarkers, multi-organ dysfunction, and worse clinical outcomes in pediatric acute respiratory failure (ARF).

Design: Retrospective cohort study.

Setting: Multicenter PICUs.

Patients: Critically ill children (2 wk to 17 yr old) receiving invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ARF, enrolled in the CAF-PINT (Coagulation and Fibrinolysis in Pediatric Insulin Titration) study (2012-2016).

Interventions: None.

Measurements and main results: A baseline RALE score was calculated for each patient from a single CXR obtained within 72 hours of IMV initiation. Among 212 patients, RALE scores demonstrated good inter-rater reliability (intra-class coefficient 0.85; 95% CI, 0.82-0.87). After adjustment for ARF etiology and illness severity, higher RALE scores were associated with fewer 28-day ventilator-free days (sub-distribution hazard ratio per 1-sd increase, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.69-0.95). Structural equation modeling demonstrated that this association was mediated through both pulmonary dysfunction, measured by the oxygenation index (β -0.14; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.22 to -0.06), and extrapulmonary organ dysfunction, measured by the Pediatric Logistic Organ Dysfunction score (β -0.05; 95% bootstrapped CI, -0.10 to -0.002). Similar associations were observed for 28-day PICU-free days. Finally, penalized regression selected soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1, intercellular adhesion molecule-1, and tumor necrosis factor receptor-1 as biomarkers associated with higher RALE scores.

Conclusions: We provide evidence that the RALE score is not solely a lung injury marker but also reflects broader systemic pathophysiology. These findings have important implications for the interpretation and clinical application of this bedside tool in pediatric ARF.

item.title: Crit Care Med: Religion and Religiosity in End-of-Life Decisions in Neurocritical Care
item.description:
Objectives: End-of-life decisions are shaped by diverse biographical, social, and cultural factors. Few studies have systematically examined the impact of religion on end-of-life decisions, and even less data are available on religiosity (i.e., strength of religious faith). The Religion and religiosity in End-of-life deCisiOns in neuroCritIcaL carE (RECONCILE) study aimed to investigate whether religiosity, rather than religion, plays a decisive role in shaping end-of-life decisions.

Design: Prospective observational study.

Setting: The study was conducted between 2021 and 2024 at two neuro-ICUs at Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin.

Patients: We prospectively studied patients with acute brain injury and poor neurologic prognosis defined by the absence of regaining decision-making capacity or sufficient autonomy. A total of 100 patients were included.

Interventions: None.

Measurements: Relatives were consulted to ascertain the patients' presumed wishes regarding the continuation or withdrawal of life-sustaining intensive care. The 10-item Santa Clara Strength of Religious Faith questionnaire was applied to measure the patient´s religiosity on a scale between 10 and 40 points. We applied the t-test for independent variables to evaluate the influence of religiosity on end-of-life decisions. To adjust for possible confounders like age, sex, nationality, and religion, we calculated a logistic regression as well as an analysis of variance calculation.

Main results: In patients in whom intensive care was continued, the median score was significantly higher compared with patients in whom intensive care was withdrawn (28.1 ± 9.0 vs. 20.5 ± 8.3; p < 0.001; Cohens d = 0.875). This finding was reproduced in each denominational group. Religion, age, and sex showed no significant association with the end-of-life decision behavior. Germans chose withdrawal of therapy significantly more often than non-Germans (p = 0.01) but also showed significantly lower religiosity scores (21.9 vs. 27.9; p = 0.003).

Conclusions: The RECONCILE study demonstrates that religiosity looks more important in influencing end-of-life decisions than religion. Higher levels of religiosity were associated with a preference for more aggressive treatment, even when neurologic prognosis is poor.

item.title: Acad Emerg Med: Subclinical Left Ventricular Hypertrophy Among Emergency Department Patients With Elevated Blood Pressure
item.category: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
item.description:
Background: Hypertension (HTN) is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, yet early detection of target organ damage is often missed, particularly in patients with limited access to care. The Emergency Department (ED), a key site of care for underserved populations, may offer an opportunity for risk stratification; we sought to determine the prevalence of LVH-a marker of subclinical disease and increased cardiovascular risk-among ED patients with asymptomatic elevated blood pressure and assess differences by sex, race, and insurance status.

Methods: We enrolled a convenience sample of adults aged 18-65 years presenting to an academic ED with blood pressure ≥ 140 mmHg systolic or ≥ 90 mmHg diastolic on two measurements. Subjects with prior LVH, active cardiac disease, hypertensive emergency, dialysis dependence, or pregnancy were excluded. LVH was identified using left ventricular mass indexed to height2.7 or body surface area via focused (point-of-care) cardiac ultrasound (parasternal long-axis view). Multivariate logistic regression assessed associations with LVH.

Results: Among 155 subjects, 46 (29.7%, 95% CI 22.5%-36.9%) had LVH. Mean age was 46.9 ± 12.1 years; 53.6% were women. LVH was more prevalent in women (38.6% vs. 19.4%; p = 0.009) and remained independently associated with female sex (OR 2.44, 95% CI 1.14-5.22, p = 0.021) and prior hypertension (OR 2.47, 95% CI 1.14-5.39, p = 0.023). Notably, 18.3% of patients without a prior hypertension diagnosis demonstrated LVH (p = 0.004).

Conclusion: Nearly one-third of ED patients with elevated blood pressure had LVH, including many without known hypertension, with a higher prevalence among women.

item.title: Crit Care: Tailored strategies for vitamin C, D, iron, and carnitine in critical illness
item.description:
Background: Micronutrients are essential cofactors for metabolic, immune, and cellular processes. Low plasma concentrations are frequent in ICU patients but poorly reflect tissue stores. Inflammation drives redistribution and utilisation, while disease, reduced intake, impaired absorption, dilution, and increased losses may contribute to true deficiency. Plasma values, therefore, cannot distinguish redistribution from deficiency, making individualised requirement estimation difficult. This narrative review focuses on four micronutrients of recent high interest, aiming to address some missing links in critical illness.

Main body: Current guidelines recommend routine provision of basal micronutrient requirements for all ICU patients, with additional monitoring and increased doses reserved for high-risk groups with losses. Plasma measurements, often the only available tool, should be interpreted alongside inflammatory markers, clinical context, and risk factors. Large RCTs of vitamin C have mainly yielded neutral or negative results, which may reflect unguided supplementation across heterogeneous populations without accounting for timing, duration, dosing strategies, and biochemical formulation variability; alternatively, vitamin C may simply be ineffective as an early intervention in critical illness. Available evidence from ICU vitamin D trials indicates signals of outcome benefit, but the evidence is heterogeneous and trial sizes are limited, preventing firm ICU-specific recommendations. Ongoing large trials are expected to clarify effects of high-dose strategies. Iron status spans a narrow therapeutic window: iron deficiency and anaemia are highly prevalent during and after ICU, yet iron overload and ferroptosis-related toxicity also contribute to organ dysfunction. Targeted, hepcidin-guided intravenous (I.V.) iron therapy appears promising to safely correct deficiency. Both carnitine deficiency and high blood levels are associated with worse outcomes in ICU patients. Risk factors for alterations in carnitine concentrations include CRRT, renal and hepatic dysfunction, valproate use, inflammation, and wound losses. Supplementation should be evaluated in a stepwise approach to detect potentially excessive levels in a dose-finding RCT.

Conclusion: New biomarkers and analytical approaches are needed to differentiate redistribution from deficiency, capturing dynamic changes over time. Future approaches should move beyond plasma measurements toward cellular and functional biomarkers that better reflect stores and biological activity. Given current limitations, testing should be selective to where results are expected to alter management, include CRP, and timing guided by underlying risk. Research should prioritise precision strategies with better biomarkers and longitudinal sampling to account for dynamic risk, needs, losses, and responses.

item.title: Crit Care: Bacteriological profiling and antimicrobial resistance of combat-related infections: analysis of war wounds from Ukraine during 2024-2025
item.description:
Background: Combat-related wound infections in the Russo-Ukrainian war pose high morbidity due to the prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) organisms. The aim of the study was to characterize pathogen distribution, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) dynamics, and risk factors (evacuation and sampling timing) with the intent to develop a prognostic model for resistance in wounded military personnel.

Patients and methods: A retrospective analysis of 203 patients with ballistic injuries treated at a Role 3 military hospital (Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine) was performed. Microbiological sampling yielded 685 unique strains. Isolates were categorized by year (2024 vs. 2025), sampling timing (≤ 48 h vs. > 48 h), and evacuation interval (< 72 h vs. ≥ 72 h). Susceptibility testing followed EUCAST v.14-15. Bacteriological profiling was made for Multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria, Extensively Drug-Resistant (XDR), and Pan-drug-Resistant (PDR) microbes. Data was managed in WHONET Microbiology Laboratory Database Software (2025); statistical analyses used R and AMR packages. A supervised machine-learning workflow using a standard Random Forest algorithm was implemented to predict phenotypic resistance risk, with model performance evaluated by ROC-AUC analysis.

Results: Gram-negative bacteria predominated, led by A. baumannii, K. pneumoniae, E. coli, and E. cloacae. Overall resistance rate was 51.2%. True patient-level carbapenem resistance was high in K. pneumoniae (imipenem 83.1%) and A. baumannii (imipenem 91.5%); colistin retained activity. Patient-corrected MDR prevalence significantly escalated from 72.9% in 2024 to 82.3% in 2025 (p = 0.022), confirming a deepening ecological resistance reservoir. Polymicrobial infections were common (93.6% of episodes), often including MDR/XDR pathogens. Resistance was highest in the early-evacuation/early-sampling (Groups 1, 73.6% MDR) and late-evacuation/late-sampling (Groups 4, 97.1% MDR) groups. Random Forest predicted resistance with an overall AUC = 0.718, demonstrating reliable performance specifically within high-volume cohorts (Groups 1 and 4).

Conclusions: Combat wounds demonstrate a severe burden of resistant Gram-negative pathogens with stationary chronological resistance plateaus linked to evacuation and sampling timelines. The rapid colonization kinetics observed during early transit continuum indicate that the institutional reservoir is pervasive across the evacuation network. The machine-learning model provides reliable automated risk stratification for high-volume echelons to optimize empirical selection, while early clinical management must prioritize aggressive surgical debridement and source control over premature antimicrobial escalation.

item.title: Resuscitation: Survival after neonatal chest compressions at birth: Temporal trends and prognostic factors in a population-based cohort, Queensland, Australia
item.description:
Aim: To examine temporal trends and prognostic factors for 28-day survival among infants receiving chest compressions (CC) in Queensland, Australia.

Methods: We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using the Queensland Perinatal Data Collection (2008-2024), including all liveborn CC recipients at birth. Temporal trends in crude 28-day survival were examined overall and by gestational age (GA) groups. Multivariable generalised estimating equations were used to identify factors independently associated with survival while accounting for clustering within birthing locations.

Results: Among 3,077 CC recipients, 70.5% established regular spontaneous breathing within 60 minutes of birth, and 89.0% survived to 28 days. Crude 28-day survival improved from 82% in 2008 to 89% in 2024 and was consistently higher in term (GA ≥37+0 weeks) than preterm infants. Compared with term infants, adjusted odds of survival declined with decreasing GA: 32+0 to 36+6 weeks (aOR 0.56, 95% CI 0.40-0.77), 28+0 to 31+6 weeks (aOR 0.35, 95% CI 0.23-0.54), and <28+0 weeks (aOR 0.17, 95% CI 0.12-0.23). However, after adjusting for cord pH or epinephrine administration, survival in infants born at 32+0 to 36+6 weeks did not differ significantly from term infants.

Conclusion: Survival to 28 days among CC recipients was high and increased over time. Lower gestational age was the strongest independent prognostic factor for mortality, although the survival difference between term and moderate-to-late preterm infants was attenuated after adjustment for cord pH or epinephrine administration. Prospective studies assessing CC indications and measures of resuscitation quality are needed to optimise neonatal resuscitation and improve outcomes.

item.title: Resuscitation: Survival after out of hospital cardiac arrest in relation to AED usage in a multi response system including AED equipped drones
item.description:
Background: Early defibrillation is a key determinant of survival in out‑of‑hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA). In multi-response systems, it remains unclear which responders contribute most to early AED use and survival. This study compared first AED-attaching responders and their association with 30-day survival in a regional multi-response system.

Methods: This registry‑based cohort study included OHCA cases in Västra Götaland Region, Sweden, between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024. Data were obtained from EMS, dispatch, and registry databases. The primary outcome was 30‑day survival.

Results: Among 9,413 OHCAs, EMS attached the first AED in 72% of cases, followed by on-duty first responders (ODFR) (18%), bystanders (6.0%), and community first responders (CFR) (4.5%). EMS attachment decreased from 77% to 67%, whereas CFR involvement increased from 1% to 13%. 30‑day survival was highest when AEDs were attached by bystanders (28%), compared with 9.0% for EMS, 8.7% for ODFR and 8.6% for CFR. Among witnessed OHCAs with an initial shockable rhythm, 30-day survival was highest in bystander-attached cases (62%), compared with 36% for CFR, 32% for ODFR, and 24% for EMS. In the multivariable analysis, bystander AED attachment was associated with higher odds of 30‑day survival compared with EMS (OR 2.25; 95% CI 1.77-2.85).

Conclusion: In this multi-response system, survival was highest when AEDs were first attached by bystanders and remained higher after adjustment for known prognostic factors. This association likely reflects earlier access to defibrillation. These findings suggest that improving immediate access to defibrillation may have the greatest impact on OHCA outcomes.

item.title: Resuscitation: Early Prehospital Prediction of Neurological Outcome After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Derivation and External Validation of the MIRA-29 Score
item.description:
Introduction: Out-of-hospital cardiac (OHCA) arrest is a frequent emergency, and few patients will survive with good neurological outcome. Identification of patients with a low likelihood of meaningful recovery represents a major clinical challenge. Numerous scores have been developed to guide decision-making after OHCA, with variable goals and targets, but most of them have been validated on small cohorts, integrates variables not available in the prehospital field, or do have low prediction values. MIRA-29 score aimed to only rely on simple clinical variables, available in the prehospital setting. We hypothetized that such score will provide incremental neurological prognosis value at an early-stage following OHCA.

Methods: MIRA-29 score was derived and internally validated over a five-year period on a prospective cohort of 1099 adult patients, including all OHCA treated by our territory dispatch center. Multivariate analysis identified independent variables within the database, that were used to optimize the prediction model using machine-learning and genetic algorithms. The score was subsequently validated externally on 82 696 patients extracted from the French national cardiac arrest registry (RéAC).

Results: Out from the 1099 patients, 85 patients (7.7%) had a favorable neurological outcome. Multivariate analysis identified five independent variables associated with neurological outcome: age, low-flow duration, number of external electric shock, epinephrine dose, and the OHCA site (street, public facility, home). After model optimization and machine-learning, age was not retained within the final model. External validation depicted a precision of 0.86 and a recall of 0.88 of the model. The F1-Score and accuracy are respectively 0.87 and 0.88, and specificity for a bad neurological prognosis is 0.99.

Conclusion: MIRA‑29 strength lies on its ability to reliably identify patients with extremely high probability of poor neurological outcome, while being based on four simple clinical variables. The prospective validation of MIRA-29 in the clinical setting may evaluate its impact on clinical decision making.

item.title: Resuscitation: RescQ(TM): One-year implementation and feasibility results of a digitally enabled support pathway for bystanders of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
item.description:
Background: Bystanders to out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) are at significant risk of psychological distress, yet no standardised support pathway exists for them in the UK. RescQ™ is a digital-first bystander support pathway embedded within regional prehospital and cardiac arrest care services.

Aim: To evaluate the feasibility of embedding RescQ™ into routine emergency medical services (EMS) practice leading to appropriate contact with bystanders involved in OHCA. Secondary aims were to describe digital access, demand for liaison officer (LO) support, identification of younger bystanders, and EMS clinician acceptability.

Methods: Prospective one-year regional service evaluation of RescQ™ across Essex, UK. Bystanders involved in eligible OHCA events were registered by EMS clinicians and provided with immediate access to secure digital resources. Bystanders could self-refer for additional support through LO.

Results: During the one-year evaluation, 220 of 432 eligible OHCA incidents had at least one bystander identified and the incident entered into the RescQ™ pathway, representing an incident-level capture rate of 50.9%. Across these incidents, 298 bystanders were identified, of whom 260 eligible adults were registered with RescQ™. Of registered adult bystanders, 96.2% accessed the digital resources at least once. Among all identified bystanders, 30/298 (10.1%) were aged under 18 years. Approximately 10% of registered bystanders self-referred for additional personalised LO support. Among 25 EMS clinician survey respondents who had used RescQTM in clinical practice, ratings indicated acceptability.

Conclusion: RescQ™ demonstrated the feasibility of identifying and supporting bystanders following OHCA through a digitally enabled pathway, achieving incident-level capture above the pre-specified feasibility threshold and high website access among registered adults. These findings support further multi-region evaluation of implementation, sustainability and scalability across different EMS systems.

item.title: Resuscitation: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrests due to foreign body airway obstruction: A CanROC registry, retrospective cohort study
item.description:
Background: Foreign body airway obstruction (FBAO) is a treatable cause of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but North American data are limited.

Methods: Exploratory retrospective cohort study of EMS-treated OHCAs using the Canadian Resuscitation Outcomes Consortium (CanROC) registry (2005-2023), classified as obviously FBAO-related or of no obvious cause (presumed cardiac). Logistic regression compared Utstein characteristics between etiologies and identified factors associated with prehospital return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) and survival to acute care discharge.

Results: Among 105,178 EMS-treated OHCAs, 1,106(1.1%) were obviously FBAO-related. Compared with cases of no obvious cause, obviously FBAO-related cases were older (median 73 vs 68 years, p<0.001), more often witnessed (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.98[5.36-9.25]), more often attended by trained bystanders (aOR 3.30[2.41-4.41]), and less often had a shockable rhythm (aOR 0.11[0.07-0.15]). Obviously FBAO-related cases more often achieved prehospital ROSC (62.7% vs 37.8%; OR 2.77[2.44-3.13]), but survival did not differ (10.6% vs 9.0%,p=0.094). Within the obviously FBAO-related cohort, ROSC was associated with witnessed arrest (aOR 1.66[1.13-2.43]) and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.95 per minute[0.92-0.99]). Survival was associated with younger age (aOR 0.76 per decade[0.61-0.93]), initial shockable rhythm (aOR 4.76[1.55-13.30]), and shorter EMS response time (aOR 0.81 per minute[0.66-0.98]). Survival was 18.1% and 0.8% among obviously FBAO-related OHCAs with and without prehospital ROSC, respectively.

Conclusions: Obviously FBAO-related OHCAs are uncommon but clinically distinct. ROSC is frequent, yet survival remains low and is associated with early prehospital factors, supporting choking prevention initiatives, bystander training, and rapid EMS response.

item.title: Resuscitation: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest
item.description:
Objectives: Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images.

Methods: Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy.

Results: Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort.

Conclusion: In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

item.title: Resuscitation: Community First Responder Activation Reduces the Negative Impact of AED Distance on Bystander Defibrillation After Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
item.description:
Introduction: Early defibrillation is critical for survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), yet bystander defibrillation remains uncommon despite the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs). We investigated whether HeartRunner community first responder activation increased the likelihood of bystander defibrillation and 30-day survival in relation to the distance to the nearest accessible AED.

Methods: Linking data from the Danish Cardiac Arrest Registry, Danish AED Network, and HeartRunner application, we identified patients with OHCA eligible for HeartRunner activation during 2017-2021. Using street-network distances to the nearest accessible AED, we examined associations between HeartRunner activation, bystander defibrillation, and 30-day survival using multivariable logistic regression with interaction terms and targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE).

Results: Among 5,753 OHCAs (median age, 74 years; 64% male; 78% in private locations), HeartRunner activation (41%) was associated with higher bystander defibrillation across AED distances (p-interaction = 0.004), with no interaction for 30-day survival (p-interaction = 0.054). Predicted bystander defibrillation with versus without HeartRunner activation was 9.6% vs 5.5% at Q1 (389 m), 10.0% vs 4.3% at median (717 m), and 13.0% vs 4.8% at Q3 (1,183 m). TMLE estimated a 6.1-percentage-point higher probability of bystander defibrillation (95% CI, 4.5-7.8; p<0.001) and a modest 1.8-percentage-point increase in 30-day survival (95% CI, 0.1-3.6; p=0.038) with HeartRunner activation.

Conclusion: HeartRunner activation attenuated the decline in bystander defibrillation with increasing AED distance following OHCA, without a corresponding distance interaction for 30-day survival. Overall, TMLE supported higher bystander defibrillation and suggested a modest increase in 30-day survival with HeartRunner activation.

item.title: Lancet: Natural ligand-based CAR T-cell therapy targeting BCMA and TACI for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (TriPRIL): a non-randomised, phase 1, first-in-human trial
item.description:
Background: Functional loss of B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a recognised mechanism of relapse after BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Targeting multiple tumour antigens simultaneously with a single CAR has the potential to mitigate antigen escape and prolong disease responses. Transmembrane activator and CAML interactor (TACI) and BCMA are both highly expressed on most myeloma cells and bind to the same natural ligand-a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). We designed TriPRIL, a CAR that uses an engineered trimeric form of APRIL, to target both BCMA and TACI. We aimed to establish the safety, tolerability, preliminary efficacy, and recommended phase 2 dose of autologous TriPRIL CAR T cells.

Methods: In this first-in-human, open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion, phase 1 study, we evaluated TriPRIL in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients had received at least three previous lines of therapy or had triple-class refractory disease. Previous CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibody therapy exposure were permitted. Patients received 3 days of lymphodepletion with intravenous cyclophosphamide (300 mg/m2) and intravenous fludarabine (30 mg/m2) daily on days -5, -4, and -3 before intravenous TriPRIL infusion on day 0. In the dose escalation phase, patients received 1·0 × 108 or 3·0 × 108 TriPRIL CAR T cells to establish the recommended phase 2 dose, which was further evaluated in the dose expansion phase. The primary endpoint was the incidence of study-related adverse events (graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5) and dose-limiting toxicities in all patients who received an infusion of TriPRIL CAR T cells, until study completion at 24 months or progressive disease. The data cutoff date was March 24, 2026, when all infused patients had completed at least one assessment of disease response. This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05020444), has fully accrued, and is ongoing.

Findings: Between Sept 17, 2021, and Jan 27, 2026, 16 patients were enrolled and underwent leukapheresis, with 15 patients subsequently receiving a TriPRIL cell infusion. Ten (67%) of 15 infused patients were female, five (33%)were male, and the median age was 69 years (IQR 65-75). Nine (60%) of 15 infused patients had previously received BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy, and four (27%) had previously received a BCMA-directed or GPRC5D-directed bispecific T-cell engager. Six patients were treated with 1·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and nine were treated with 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells; there were no dose-limiting toxicities at either dose. The most common adverse events were neutropenia (14 [93%] of 15 patients), nausea (12 [80%]), hypogammaglobulinaemia (eight [53%]), fatigue (seven [47%]), and fever (seven [47%]). Non-haematological adverse events grade 3 or worse occurred in five (33%) patients and all resolved. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1 or 2 only) occurred in 13 (87%, 95% CI 60-98) infused patients. One (7%, 0-32) patient had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, and one (7%, 0-32) had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome; both of these patients had received 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and both conditions resolved with corticosteroids. Infections occurred in six (40%, 16-68) infused patients, with a grade 3 infection in one patient (7%, 0-32). There were no treatment-related deaths. The recommended phase 2 dose of CAR T cells was set as 3·0 × 108 cells.

Interpretation: TriPRIL showed a favourable safety profile and warrants further investigation in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including those previously treated with BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy. The study findings support further development of this dual-targeted, natural ligand-based CAR T-cell approach.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: A Mobile Application Improves Paramedic Performance in Simulated Trauma Care: A Crossover Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description:
Objectives: Clinical performance during prehospital trauma care varies among emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, particularly during high-stress critical responses. We developed a mobile application providing real-time access to local treatment protocols, decision support tools, and instructional procedure videos to supplement standard practice. We evaluated whether use of the application improved paramedic performance during simulated trauma scenarios.

Methods: We conducted a crossover randomized controlled trial between July 2025 and February 2026 comparing standard care alone with standard care plus the mobile application during two high-fidelity trauma simulations (one adult and one pediatric). Paramedics, working in pairs, were block randomized to one of four sequences, varying both the scenario order and the application use. Performance was assessed using predefined critical actions; completing all critical actions was required to successfully complete the scenario. A generalized linear mixed model with a binomial distribution and logit link function was used for each paramedic pair to estimate the adjusted odds ratio (OR) for successfully completing a scenario with or without the application.

Results: Of 112 paramedics, 98 (88%) participated, forming 49 pairs. One pair withdrew before study completion, leaving 48 pairs for analysis. For scenarios using the application, 17/48 (35.4%) successfully completed the scenario compared to 3/48 (6.3%) for scenarios not using the application, adjusted odds 8.28 (95% CI 2.21-31.09). Among scenarios using the application, 10/25 (40%) adult scenarios and 7/23 (30.4%) pediatric scenarios met successful completion criteria compared to 3/23 (13%) adult and 0/25 (0%) pediatric with standard practice alone. User experience survey results demonstrated that participating paramedics assessed the application as being practical to use and valuable for clinical care.

Conclusions: Use of the mobile decision support application improves odds of performing high-quality clinical care in simulated trauma patient scenarios. Further studies are needed to evaluate performance and usability in a field environment.
