item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Five-Year Experience with Automated Head Up Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
item.description:
Objectives: Automated head-up position cardiopulmonary resuscitation (AHUP-CPR), the combination of a head and thorax positioning device, active compression-decompression CPR, and an impedance threshold device, lowers intracranial pressure and increases cerebral blood flow and neurologically favorable survival in animal models versus conventional CPR (C-CPR).

Methods: This prospective, observational, investigator-initiated registry study reports 5-year multi-center outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) from areas served by emergency medical services (EMS) agencies that implemented AHUP-CPR as their routine first-responder standard of care. Adults with non-traumatic OHCA were initially treated with immediate conventional (C-CPR) followed by rapid transition to AHUP-CPR. The primary study focus was on patients who survived to hospital discharge with favorable neurological function (HD-FN). Additional analyses included assessment of sustained return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC), survival to hospital discharge (HD), outcomes based upon the presenting rhythm, and impact of covariates on HD-FN.

Results: Ten EMS agencies serving 1.5 million people across nine U.S. states contributed data to the AHUP-CPR Registry. A total of 3,709 OHCA patients met enrollment criteria. Across five years, (2020-2024), the average (± SD) interval from 9-1-1 call receipt-to-professional CPR was 9.62 ± 5.78 min. Incidence of ROSC, HD, and HD-FN were 29.5%, 13.1%, and 10.5%, respectively. The incidence of HD-FN for patients presenting with a shockable rhythm meeting Utstein criteria, pulseless electrical activity, or asystole were 33.9%, 11.8%, and 2.0%, respectively. Among 391 neurologically favorable survivors, 91% had a Cerebral Performance Category score of 1 (normal or near normal brain function) at HD. The average age of the survivors was 56.8 ± 16.3 years. Age, interval from 9-1-1 call to professional CPR, witnessed status, and initial rhythm were the most significant predictors of HD-FN using multivariable Poisson regression.

Conclusions: In this 5-year observational registry study, use of AHUP-CPR for the treatment of OHCA was associated with survival to HD of 13.1% and HD-FN of 10.5% in the overall cohort, which comprised patients presenting in shockable rhythms, PEA, and asystole. Drawn from 3,709 OHCA patients treated across diverse EMS systems, these findings provide the largest clinical practice-based characterization to date of the outcomes associated with early transition to AHUP-CPR.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Prehospital Resource Utilization After Video-Assisted Versus Telephone-Only Emergency Calls: A Post Hoc Analysis of the CAM-VISION Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Objectives: To examine whether video assistance during emergency calls reduced actual prehospital resource utilization across the complete response pathway compared with telephone-only calls.

Methods: This post hoc analysis included 18,745 calls from the cluster-randomized CAM-VISION parent trial (NCT05742412; 8,124 video; 10,621 telephone only). Outcomes were assessed at call level according to telecommunicator allocation and included unit dispatch, pathway progression, number of units, and cumulative unit time. Effects were estimated with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) accounting for clustering by telecommunicator.

Results: Initial unit dispatch occurred in 69.4% of video-group calls and 73.9% of telephone-only calls (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% confidence intervals (CI) (-10.0 to 1.0). Among calls with no unit initially dispatched, subsequent unit dispatch was uncommon (5.1% vs 5.5%). Across the complete response pathway, 71.0% versus 75.3% received at least 1 unit (risk difference, -4.4 percentage points; 95% CI, -9.6 to 0.8), and 69.3% versus 73.8% had a unit reach the scene (risk difference, -4.5 percentage points; 95% CI, -10.0 to 1.0). More than 1 unit was dispatched in 23.3% versus 25.0%. Mean units per call were 1.005 versus 1.054 (mean difference, -0.049; 95% CI, -0.148 to 0.049); mean cumulative unit time was 52.8 versus 54.3 minutes (mean difference, -1.5; 95% CI, -6.2 to 3.1). Overall, differences in initial dispatch were concentrated in ambulance use.

Conclusions: No statistically significant absolute differences in conventional prehospital resource utilization were observed. Point estimates were consistently lower in the video group, primarily through fewer initial dispatches, and subsequent dispatch did not materially offset this numerical difference.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Clinician Acceptance of Large Language Model-Generated Discharge Summaries
item.description:
Importance: Hospital discharge summaries are essential for continuity of care, but fragmented electronic health record (EHR) data can compromise their quality and safety. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for clinical documentation tasks despite limited evidence regarding their performance in health care settings compared with the current standard of care.

Objective: To evaluate clinician acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries derived from EHRs compared with routine clinician-written summaries.

Design, setting, and participants: In this retrospective comparative effectiveness study using a prespecified noninferiority framework, acceptability of LLM-generated discharge summaries was compared with clinician-authored discharge summaries. Admission records from 5 London hospitals for September 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, were evaluated against the full admission record by practicing physicians. Admissions were eligible only if the clinician-authored discharge summary contained identifiable clinical summary, plan and requested actions, and information given sections. Data analysis was conducted from July 2025 to February 2026.

Intervention: LLM-generated summaries were produced using GPT-4o mini (July 18, 2024 release; OpenAI) and a clinician-codesigned prompt.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was clinician signoff with no or minor edits, derived from 2 sequential questions: (1) whether the reviewer would sign the summary and (2) whether no, minor, or major edits were required. A 5-percentage-point noninferiority margin was prespecified. Secondary outcomes assessed accuracy, completeness, tone, and clarity (using a 5-point Likert scale: 1, poor; 2, fair; 3, good; 4, very good; and 5, excellent) and potential harmfulness of missing or incorrect information (using a 5-point Likert scale: 1, no harm; 2, minor harm; 3, moderate harm; 4, high harm; and 5, extremely high harm).

Results: The study sample included 1294 (649 clinician-authored and 645 LLM-generated) unique case discharge summaries that were evaluated against the full admission record by 12 practicing physicians. Case patients had a median age of 46.0 years (IQR, 26.2-69.8 years), 733 (56.6%) were assigned female at birth, and the median length of stay was 3.0 days (IQR, 1.0-7.0 days). The absolute difference in model-estimated probability of signoff with no or minor edits (LLM generated minus clinician authored) was 22.2 percentage points (95% CI, 19.0-27.5 percentage points); the lower bound exceeded the prespecified noninferiority margin of -5 percentage points, demonstrating noninferiority. LLM-generated summaries received higher ratings for accuracy, completeness, tone, and clarity (adjusted risk differences for scores ≥4 ranged from 19.4 [95% CI, 14.8-24.1] to 29.1 [95% CI, 25.1-33.6] percentage points; all 95% CIs excluded 0). LLM-generated summaries also had a lower proportion of cases rated 3 or greater for potential harm on the clinical summary and plan and requested actions sections (140 of 534 [26.2%] and 124 of 462 [26.8%]) compared with clinician-authored summaries (271 of 601 [45.1%] and 278 of 540 [51.5%]).

Conclusions and relevance: In this study, LLM-generated discharge summaries met the current standard of care, representing a promising early use case for generative artificial intelligence in health care with close clinician oversight.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Timing of Antenatal Care, Stillbirth, and Infant Mortality in Migrant Mothers in Australia
item.description:
Importance: Timely antenatal care (ANC) reduces pregnancy risks, yet the association between delayed ANC and stillbirth or infant mortality among migrant mothers in Australia has not previously been investigated.

Objective: To examine whether delayed ANC is associated with higher stillbirth and infant mortality among Australia-born compared with migrant mothers.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective cohort study assessed births to non-Indigenous mothers in New South Wales from January 1, 2002, to December 31, 2020, followed up to infant age of 1 year. Mothers were categorized as Australia-born, migrant from English-speaking country (ESM), or migrant from non-English-speaking country (non-ESM). Data were analyzed between August 2025 and June 2026.

Exposures: Timing of first ANC, defined as 12 weeks or earlier, 13 to 19 weeks, 20 weeks or later, or no ANC.

Main outcomes and measures: The main outcome was stillbirth (at ≥20 weeks) and infant mortality (at prehospital discharge, posthospital discharge, or 1 year). Adjusted relative risks (ARRs) were estimated using Poisson regression models, stratified by migration group.

Results: This study included 1 720 033 births (median [IQR] maternal age, 31.2 [27.4-34.8] years; 884 235 male infants [51.4%]), including 1 132 193 (65.8%) to Australia-born, 116 026 (6.7%) to ESM, and 471 814 (27.4%) to non-ESM mothers. Late ANC (>12 weeks) was more common in non-ESM mothers (190 338 [40.3%]) than Australia-born (334 790 [29.6%]) or ESM (41 029 [35.4%]) mothers. In cross-group comparisons, non-ESM mother status was associated with higher risk of adverse outcomes regardless of ANC timing. Compared with Australia-born mothers with early ANC (≤12 weeks), a higher risk of stillbirth (ARR, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.18-1.33) and 1-year (ARR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.22-1.44), predischarge (ARR, 1.39; 95% CI, 1.25-1.54), and postdischarge (ARR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.03-1.37) infant mortality was observed in non-ESM mothers accessing ANC by 12 weeks. Similar risk patterns were observed in non-ESM mothers with late ANC. In within-group comparisons, among Australia-born mothers, each category of delayed ANC was associated with higher risk. No ANC was associated with the highest risks across all maternal groups for stillbirth and 1-year infant mortality. For non-ESM mothers, late ANC (≥20 weeks) was associated with a lower risk of predischarge mortality (ARR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.61-0.92) but a higher risk of postdischarge mortality (ARR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.02-1.65).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 1.72 million births, higher risks of stillbirths and infant mortalities were observed in non-ESM mothers regardless of ANC timing, warranting further investigation.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Neighborhood Deprivation and Developmental Concerns Across Early Childhood
item.description:
Importance: Neighborhood deprivation is an important environmental context for understanding child development and has been linked in extensive prior work with physical and cognitive outcomes. However, neighborhood deprivation is understudied in relation to socioemotional development in early childhood, a critical period for prevention and intervention.

Objective: To examine prospective associations between neighborhood deprivation and children's socioemotional development from infancy to preschool age and to test whether associations differ by race.

Design, setting, and participants: In this longitudinal cohort study, participants were mother-child dyads with available neighborhood and socioemotional assessment data who were recruited in April 2020 from the greater Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, area as part of a longitudinal cohort within a large health system. Assessments were conducted at child ages 1, 2, and 4 years. Data collection started in June 2021 for children aged 1 year and in May 2024 for children aged 4 years and ended in March 2025.

Exposure: A composite neighborhood deprivation index derived from objective US census-based measures linked to participants' residential addresses, including the Child Opportunity Index, Area Deprivation Index, Social Vulnerability Index, and Heat Vulnerability Index.

Main outcomes and measures: Parent-reported developmental concerns from Ages and Stages Questionnaires: Social-Emotional, Second Edition (ASQ:SE-2) scores at each age and electronic health record (EHR) data on developmental or behavioral diagnoses.

Results: The analytic sample included 249 mother-child dyads; 125 children (50.2%) were female. A total of 130 households (52.2%) were included in the White group and 118 (47.8%) in the Black or multiracial group. Greater neighborhood deprivation was associated with more parent-reported socioemotional concerns (β = 0.29 [95% CI, 0.20-0.38]; P < .001), independent of family income and maternal anxiety. Children from more deprived neighborhoods had increased odds of being referred for monitoring or intervention (odds ratio [OR], 2.43 [95% CI, 1.05-5.64]; P = .04). A similar pattern was observed for developmental or behavioral diagnoses in children's electronic health records (OR, 1.40 [95% CI, 1.01-2.01]; P = .050). The magnitude of these associations was greater among children from Black or multiracial households, who lived in significantly more deprived neighborhoods than children from White households (χ21 = 304.62; P < .001).

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study, neighborhood deprivation was associated with worse socioemotional functioning across early childhood, above and beyond family-level factors. Children from Black or multiracial compared with White households lived in neighborhoods with greater disadvantage, emphasizing underlying structural inequities and the importance of community-level investment and equitable urban planning to support early developmental health and equity.

item.title: Ann Emerg Med: Ultrasound-Guided Suprascapular Nerve Block Versus Intravenous Fentanyl for Analgesia in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department With Traumatic Scapular Fractures
item.description:
Study objective: To compare the analgesic efficacy and safety of ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block with intravenous fentanyl in patients with traumatic scapular fractures.

Methods: We conducted an open-label randomized controlled pilot trial in the emergency department (ED) of a Level I trauma center in North India. Adults with traumatic scapular fractures and Defense and Veterans Pain Rating Scale scores of 7 and higher, were randomly assigned to ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block or intravenous fentanyl (1 μg/kg). Pain scores were assessed at baseline and 30, 60, 120, 240, and 360 minutes. Secondary outcomes included rescue analgesia and adverse events.

Results: Sixty patients were randomly assigned to the 2 groups. Median baseline pain score was 10 in both groups. Pain scores were consistently lower with suprascapular nerve block, with median scores of 3 (interquartile [IQR] 2 to 5) versus 7 (IQR 6 to 8) at 30 minutes. Between-group differences were 4 (95% confidence interval [CI], 3 to 4) at 30 and 60 minutes, 2 (95% CI, 2 to 2) at 120 and 240 minutes, and 1 (95% CI, 1 to 2) at 360 minutes. Rescue analgesia was less frequent with suprascapular nerve block (13% versus 79%; risk difference, -66% [95% CI, 47.5 to 85.2]). Drowsiness was more common with fentanyl (12 versus 2 participants); hypotension occurred in 1 fentanyl recipient and paresthesia in 1 suprascapular nerve block recipient.

Conclusion: In this pilot randomized trial, ultrasound-guided suprascapular nerve block provided greater and sustained pain relief, reduced rescue analgesia, and fewer systemic adverse effects than intravenous fentanyl in adults with traumatic scapular fractures. Larger multicenter trials are needed to confirm these findings and evaluate cumulative opioid use and longer-term outcomes.

item.title: JAMA: Toward a Healthier Future Through Obesity Prevention and Care: The JAMA Summit Report on Obesity
item.description:
Importance: Obesity is one of the most difficult challenges of the modern era, affecting more than 1 billion people worldwide. Nearly half of US adults and 1 in 5 US children meet the medical definition of having obesity, with major consequences for cardiometabolic, kidney, hepatic, pulmonary, musculoskeletal, reproductive, oncologic, and mental health. Obesity also carries social and economic harms through stigma, discrimination, and bias.

Observations: Drivers of the obesity epidemic include changes in food production and consumption accompanied by social, economic, and technological shifts that reduce food preparation, disrupt sleep, and decrease physical activity. The burden of these changes is not equally distributed, with higher obesity prevalence among socioeconomically disadvantaged populations. Current prevention measures include nutrition standards, food and menu labeling, school meal policies, sugar-sweetened beverage taxes, community-based lifestyle programs, and public assistance efforts. The impact of these approaches has been inadequate. Contemporary clinical management recognizes obesity as a chronic disease characterized by genetic, biological, and behavioral susceptibilities. Access, affordability, tolerability, and the chronicity of use remain major challenges for all available obesity management strategies, including new glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapies. Potential solutions require a coordinated, multisector response and include efforts to prevent obesity at the societal level, improve care of individuals with obesity, and strengthen research and innovation. Priority areas include improving the food and physical activity environment; strengthening communication and education; strengthening childhood obesity prevention; addressing health inequities; reducing stigma and bias; modernizing obesity care delivery; expanding access to lifestyle, healthy food, medication, and surgical interventions; and supporting long-term treatment adherence and maintenance. Proposed actions include new government policies on food production, labeling, marketing, and school nutrition; modernization of drug evaluation; payment reform to support comprehensive obesity treatment; development of multidisciplinary care models; incentives to promote cross-sector partnerships; and research to advance personalized prevention and treatment strategies.

Conclusions and relevance: The emergence of effective obesity management medications offers a significant opportunity to curb the prevalence of obesity. However, no single intervention will be enough. Sustained improvement will require addressing the underlying structural and environmental drivers of obesity, along with person-centered, multilevel strategies that simultaneously improve prevention, reduce stigma, and expand equitable access to evidence-based treatment. Coordinated action across government, health care systems, clinicians, payers, industry, schools, communities, and researchers will be essential to achieving long-term improvement.

item.title: Crit Care: Switching from controlled to assisted ventilation based on oxygenation thresholds and PEEP: a target trial emulation
item.description:
Objective: To determine whether PaO2/FiO2-based dynamic treatment strategies can optimise the timing of switching from controlled to assisted ventilation.

Design and setting: Target trial emulation using the MIMIC-IV database v3.1 (2008-2022).

Patients: Adult ICU patients on controlled invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) for ≥ 48 h with at least one PaO2/FiO2 <300 mmHg. A sensitivity analysis included patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, excluding post-surgical patients.

Interventions: We compared strategies defined by switching once PaO2/FiO2 exceeded predefined thresholds (150, 200, or 250 mmHg). Additionally, to account for possible PEEP-dependent effects, the thresholds were evaluated depending on the set PEEP (< 8 vs. ≥8 cmH2O), yielding nine strategies. Outcomes were 28-day restricted mean time lost (RMTL) to successful extubation (where a lower RMTL indicates a longer time to extubation) and mortality.

Measurements and main results: Among 1,635 patients, the strategy of delaying the switch until PaO2/FiO2 >250 mmHg showed a longer time to successful extubation compared to switching at > 150 mmHg or > 200 mmHg (RMTL 17.4 days [95% CI: 15.9-18.6] vs. 19.6 days [95% CI: 18.6-20.9] and 19.8 days [95% CI: 18.5-21.1], respectively). Exploratory PEEP-dependent analyses demonstrated the longest time to successful extubation with '>250 mmHg' for both low and high PEEP and the shortest with '>150 mmHg for low PEEP; >200 mmHg for high PEEP'. Among patients ventilated for ≥ 24 h, the 150 mmHg threshold was most favourable, irrespective of PEEP. No mortality differences were observed across strategies.

Conclusions: Switching as soon as PaO2/FiO2 >150 mmHg is generally favoured over delaying until > 250 mmHg. Patients requiring ≥ 48 h of controlled IMV with PEEP ≥ 8 cmH2O may potentially benefit from a slightly higher threshold (> 200 mmHg). Prospective validation is warranted.

item.title: Crit Care: Development and external validation of age-specific predictive models for sepsis in critically ill neonates and children using multidimensional hematological parameters: a multicenter retrospective study
item.description:
Background: Sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in neonatal and pediatric intensive care units (NICU/PICU). Given the rapid clinical deterioration of these vulnerable populations, shifting from reactive diagnosis to proactive prediction of sepsis onset is crucial. Multidimensional hematological parameters may provide new insights for risk stratification. While routine complete blood count (CBC) is widely used, the predictive potential of high-dimensional hematological cell morphology features that extend beyond traditional CBC remains under-investigated in large-scale pediatric cohorts.

Methods: This multicenter study utilized a large-scale dataset from the CALM2302 project, encompassing 17,066 critically ill neonates and children across 30 Chinese hospitals between October 2020 and October 2023. We developed population-specific CatBoost models for NICU and PICU to predict sepsis onset. To mitigate class imbalance, random undersampling was applied to the training sets. From a candidate pool of 1,924 parameters (37 routine CBC and 1,887 research features), optimized signatures of approximately 200 features were selected for each population. Model performance was evaluated by the area under the ROC curve (AUC) across internal and dual external validation cohorts. Furthermore, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was performed to ensure model interpretability and identify key biological predictors.

Results: Among the total cohort, 10,347 infants were categorized into the NICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 7.48%), while 6,719 children formed the PICU cohort (sepsis incidence: 10.92%). CatBoost was identified as the optimal architecture after benchmarking nine machine learning algorithms. The population-specific simplified 18-variable models demonstrated robust performance. In the NICU cohort, the model achieved an internal AUC of 0.846 and external AUCs of 0.742 and 0.827. For the PICU cohort, corresponding AUCs were 0.803, 0.717, and 0.811. These simplified models maintained highly comparable discriminative power to the full models (range of AUC attenuation: 0.005-0.027). SHAP analysis identified 18 key predictive features for each cohort, with only two shared features between the two populations and the remaining being cohort-specific. Notably, most of these 18 features were research parameters rather than traditional blood counts indices. Furthermore, most of these features remained statistically significant in multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, sex, and study sites.

Conclusions: In this large multicenter cohort, we developed and validated simplified 18-variable models that accurately predict sepsis in both neonatal and pediatric populations. By capturing early hematological morphological alterations beyond traditional blood counts, these models offer a robust, interpretable, and clinically accessible solution for proactive sepsis management in intensive care units.

item.title: Crit Care: Ventilator-circuit configurations for noninvasive ventilation in infants with acute respiratory failure: a randomized crossover trial
item.description:
Patient-ventilator synchrony may differ across ventilator and circuit configurations during noninvasive ventilation (NIV) in infants. We compared an intentional-leak single-limb turbine configuration (SLC-turbine), a dual-limb turbine configuration with an active expiratory valve (DLC-turbine), and a dual-limb compressed-gas pediatric ICU configuration (DLC-PICU) in infants receiving NIV for acute respiratory failure METHODS: In this single-center randomized crossover physiological study, infants underwent three 30-minute NIV phases in randomized order with unchanged pressure support, PEEP, and FiO₂. Esophageal pressure was used to assess the asynchrony index (AI), individual asynchronies, and inspiratory effort. Primary and secondary endpoints were AI differences between DLC-PICU and SLC-turbine and between DLC-PICU and DLC-turbine, respectively RESULTS: Twenty infants entered stabilization, 13 were randomized, and 12 completed the protocol (age 10 [7-21] months; SpO₂/FiO₂ 185 [160-220]). AI differed across configurations: 8.6% [6.7-16.5] with SLC-turbine, 25.4% [16.3-35.0] with DLC-turbine, and 45.7% [30.5-63.8] with DLC-PICU (p=0.0023). AI was higher with DLC-PICU than with SLC-turbine (Hodges-Lehmann difference +32.0%, 95% CI +13.9 to +50.1; p=0.0015) and DLC-turbine (+18.4%, 95% CI +5.9 to +36.3; p=0.021). Ineffective efforts, double triggering, and premature cycling did not differ across configurations. All NIV configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, with no significant differences among NIV configurations CONCLUSIONS: AI was lower with SLC-turbine and DLC-turbine than with DLC-PICU and lowest with SLC-turbine. Auto-triggering showed the clearest configuration-dependent difference. All configurations reduced inspiratory effort versus unassisted spontaneous breathing, without significant between-configuration differences. Because ventilator platform, circuit and expiratory architecture, and device-specific control functions differed, effects of individual components cannot be determined. These findings are specific to the ventilators and configurations evaluated. Further studies should determine whether these physiological differences translate into improved NIV tolerance or short- and long-term clinical outcomes TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04017780. item.title: Resuscitation: Trends in United States Pediatric In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Incidence and Mortality in a Nationally Representative Sample, 2009-2022
item.description:
Aim: National estimates of pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA) incidence in the United States rely on a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative datasets offer a nationally representative alternative. We estimated nationally representative pediatric IHCA incidence and mortality trends from 2009 through 2022.

Methods: Serial cross-sectional analysis of five triennial editions of the Kids' Inpatient Database (2009-2022), identifying IHCA in children <18 years by ICD-9 (99.60, 99.63) and ICD-10 (5A12012) cardiopulmonary resuscitation procedure codes. Two hospitals with implausible CPR rates were excluded. Survey-weighted incidence per 1,000 hospitalizations and in-hospital mortality among resuscitated children were estimated overall and by neonatal status, complex chronic condition (CCC) status, ZIP-code income quartile, and US Census region. Trends were tested with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression across the full period and, as exploratory analyses, within the ICD-10 era (2016-2022).

Results: Observed IHCA incidence was 1.11/1,000 in 2009 and 1.22/1,000 in 2012, decreased to 1.11/1,000 at the ICD-10 transition and increased to 1.35/1,000 by 2022. IHCA incidence in children hospitalized with a CCC rose from 3.26 to 6.60/1,000 (6.2%/year, p<0.001), while incidence without CCC remained low. Incidence varied by socioeconomic status (lowest vs highest income quartile 1.78 vs 1.04/1,000 in 2022). In-hospital mortality ranged from 34.1% (2012) to 40.4% (2019), whereas IHCA deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased 1.7%/year (p<0.001), concentrated among children with a CCC.

Conclusion: The incidence of pediatric IHCA increased among hospitalizations involving children with CCC and was higher among children who live in lower income areas. In-hospital mortality after CPR was largely stable, whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased among children with CCC. A single hospital's coding practices can materially distort national administrative estimates. What is already known Pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest affects approximately 15,200 children annually in the United States, with this national estimate derived primarily from a voluntary registry that may underrepresent smaller and critical access hospitals. Administrative databases offer nationally representative coverage but rely on procedure codes that are susceptible to misclassification. What this study adds In this nationally representative administrative database sample spanning 2009-2022, this study demonstrated that: 1) the incidence of IHCA among children with complex chronic conditions (CCC) rose steadily and accounted for the substantial majority of events, 2) the overall IHCA incidence was higher among children who live in lower income areas with the gradient worsening over the period evaluated, and 3) in-hospital mortality after CPR increased only slightly (34-40%), whereas arrest-related deaths per 1,000 hospitalizations increased more, driven mainly by rising incidence among children with CCC, and 4) CPR coding at a single hospital can substantially distort national administrative estimates.

item.category: The American journal of emergency medicine
item.description:
Background: Management of painful vaso-occlusive crises (VOC), a hallmark of sickle cell disease (SCD), is a critical responsibility of emergency physicians (EPs). However, timely administration of opioid analgesia remains below the American Society of Hematology (ASH) 2020 guideline target.

Objectives: Our team implemented a technology-based intervention using a salmon-colored visual signal in the Electronic Health Record (EHR) to easily identify ED patients with SCD and prompt clinicians to prioritize patients with VOC. The study examined whether the intervention improved time to opioid administration for SCD VOC in a large urban academic ED.

Methods: This retrospective pre-post intervention study used EHR data for adult ED encounters with a diagnosis of SCD VOC over one year. The primary predictor was pre-intervention and post-intervention visits. Mixed-effects models examined associations between clinical outcomes and the primary predictor while accounting for repeated visits for VOC by the same patient. The primary outcome was mean time from ED arrival to first opioid administration. Secondary outcome was whether patients received the opioid within 60 min of ED arrival. A sensitivity analysis excluded high ED utilizers at various thresholds; more than 5, 10, 24, and 29 ED visits for SCD VOC.

Results: Among 841 ED encounters from 168 patients, mean time to first opioid was 66.3 min pre-intervention and 71.7 min post-intervention. Adjusted models indicated that time to first opioid administration was 2.50 min longer post-intervention (95% CI: -4.16 to 9.15). The odds of receiving first opioids within 60 min did not differ between intervention periods (aOR = 0.97, 95% CI: 0.71 to 1.32, absolute difference = 1.7, 95% CI: -5.1 to 8.4). Sensitivity analyses excluding high ED utilizers at four thresholds showed consistent results with primary analysis: 5-visit threshold (247 visits, adjusted difference = 3.4 min, 95% CI: -16.1 to 23); 10-visit threshold (377 visits, adjusted difference = 1.2 min, 95% CI: -11.6 to 14); 24-visit threshold (514 visits, adjusted difference = 4 min, 95% CI: -7.0 to 15.1); 29-visit threshold (572 visits, adjusted difference = 3.5 min, 95% CI: -6.4 to 13.3). None of these results reached statistical significance.

Conclusion: These findings suggest that passive EHR visual signals alone are insufficient to reduce analgesia delays in VOC, and that meaningful improvement will likely require multi-component, systems-based interventions integrating workflow redesign, nurse-initiated protocols, and automated clinical decision support.

item.title: Drug Alcohol Depend: "More opportunities to connect," Perspectives on integrating contingency management into peer support services from a qualitative study
item.description:
Background: Contingency management (CM), the most effective intervention for stimulant use disorder, is typically delivered by counselors rather than peer recovery support specialists. The Peer Engagement in Methamphetamine Overdose Reduction with Contingency Management (PEER-CM) study tests peer-delivered CM to reduce overdose and increase treatment engagement among people using stimulants who are not seeking treatment. This study sought to understand peer and client perspectives on integration of CM into peer services.

Methods: From October 2024 to February 2026, we conducted 26 dyadic qualitative interviews with peers (n = 18) and their clients (n = 26) and seven focus groups with peers (n = 15) and peer supervisors (n = 8) across 14 PEER-CM sites. Some peers were paired with multiple clients. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed using thematic analysis with separate codebooks for interviews and focus groups. The peer steering committee reviewed and refined preliminary themes.

Results: Both peers and clients described CM as promoting initial engagement by bringing clients "in the door," while also supporting ongoing motivation for change. CM created opportunities to build rapport and trust, strengthening relationships over time. Although peers noted occasional challenges verifying incentivized behaviors, they emphasized working "side by side" with clients and prioritizing nonjudgmental support. Peers valued the structure of CM skills and integrated them into routine practice to facilitate deeper connections.

Conclusions: Peers and their clients who use stimulants viewed peer-delivered CM positively and felt CM did not undermine the peer relationship. Integration of CM within peer support represents a promising strategy to potentially improve engagement among non-treatment seeking populations.

item.description:
Importance: Blood biomarkers that reflect neurofibrillary tau burden, a defining hallmark of Alzheimer disease (AD), remain limited. Endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding region tau 243 (eMTBR-tau243) has shown promise when measured by mass spectrometry; a scalable immunoassay could broaden research access and support clinical evaluation.

Objective: To determine whether plasma levels of eMTBR-tau measured by a novel immunoassay are associated with tau neurofibrillary tangle pathology defined by neuropathology and tau positron emission tomography (PET).

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study included brain donors with antemortem plasma from 2 US autopsy cohorts, and individuals with plasma samples and tau PET from 2 imaging cohorts in Canada and Sweden, with visits between 2002 and 2025 depending on the cohort.

Exposures: Plasma eMTBR-tau measured with an immunoassay and eMTBR-tau243 measured with mass spectrometry.

Main outcomes and measures: Plasma eMTBR-tau levels across neuropathologic Braak neurofibrillary tangle stages (I-VI, ranging from tangles confined to the entorhinal region to widespread neocortical tangles) and tau-PET Braak stages (0-VI), expressed as fold changes. Correlations with regional tau-PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs; higher values indicating more tau tangles), discrimination of regional tau-PET positivity (area under the curve [AUC]), and correlation with mass spectrometry-based eMTBR-tau243.

Results: The study included 728 participants in 4 cohorts (median age by cohort, 71.0-83.5 years; 41.3%-56.6% female). In the 2 autopsy cohorts (n = 241 and n = 240), eMTBR-tau age- and sex-adjusted geometric means were 0.0021 pg/mL and 0.0040 pg/mL, respectively, at Braak stages I-II vs 0.107 pg/mL and 0.101 pg/mL at Braak stage VI (50.5-fold [95% CI, 26.3-97.0] and 25.2-fold [95% CI, 15.8-40.3] higher for stage VI vs stages I-II; P < .001 for both cohorts). In one imaging cohort (n = 99), compared with tau-PET Braak stage 0, eMTBR-tau levels were 11.0-fold (95% CI, 6.9-17.5) higher at stages III-IV and 59.9-fold (95% CI, 39.5-90.7) higher at stages V-VI. Among participants positive for amyloid-β (Aβ) in another imaging cohort (n = 50), the Spearman rank correlations for eMTBR-tau with tau-PET SUVRs were ρ = 0.52 (95% CI, 0.28-0.70) in Braak regions I-II, 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.86) in regions III-IV, and 0.85 (95% CI, 0.75-0.91) in regions V-VI (all P < .001). Immunoassay and mass spectrometry measurements were strongly correlated (Spearman rank correlation, ρ = 0.93 in all participants [n = 108] and ρ = 0.96 in Aβ-positive participants [n = 54]) and discriminated tau-PET positivity similarly (n = 102; AUC range, 0.96-0.99 for the immunoassay and 0.97-0.99 for mass spectrometry).

Conclusions and relevance: A plasma eMTBR-tau immunoassay identified neocortical tau pathology in autopsy and tau-PET cohorts and correlated strongly with mass spectrometry measurements, a proof of principle that eMTBR-tau can be measured by immunoassay as a marker of advanced neurofibrillary tangle pathology.

item.title: Ann Intern Med: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description:
Background: Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.

Design: Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).

Setting: Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.

Participants: 132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.

Intervention: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.

Measurements: The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.

Results: At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.

Limitation: Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.

Conclusion: Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: Cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered prehospital thrombolysis for ST elevation myocardial infarction
item.description:
Objectives: Guidelines recommend prehospital thrombolysis for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) if trained clinicians can interpret 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) on site. The Queensland Ambulance Service (QAS) has a well-established prehospital reperfusion program under which all paramedics are trained in prehospital STEMI diagnosis on 12-lead ECG and administering thrombolysis in the field to eligible patients. Whilst the clinical benefits of this treatment are proven, its cost-effectiveness remains to be established.

Methods: We developed a decision-analytic microsimulation model to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of paramedic-administered thrombolysis for prehospital STEMI in the state of Queensland, Australia. The comparator was a hypothetical counterfactual group of patients who were clinically eligible for prehospital thrombolysis but received an alternate treatment pathway. The analysis was conducted from a health provider (Queensland Government) perspective. A lifetime time horizon was used. Input values of the acute phase were derived from our prehospital and linked hospital database of all STEMI patients receiving prehospital thrombolysis from QAS paramedics between January 2022 and December 2024. Input values of the long-term phase were obtained from published literature. Cost was expressed in Australian dollars (AUD) and United States dollars (USD) in 2026 value, and effectiveness in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs).

Results: Prehospital thrombolysis improved outcomes at a cost of AUD 16,750.22 per QALY gained (95% uncertainty range AUD 15,477.48 - 18,422.84) or USD 11,725.15 (USD 10,834.24 - 12,895.99). In the sensitivity analysis, the cost-effectiveness of prehospital thrombolysis was robust to changes in input values.

Conclusions: Paramedic-administered thrombolysis in the field for prehospital STEMI, compared with no such treatment, represents value for money.

item.title: Prehosp Emerg Care: A Lighter Approach to Language Access: Virtual Interpreter Utilization in Emergency Medical Services (EMS)
item.description:
Objectives: Limited English Proficiency (LEP) may create communication barriers during prehospital care. Although on-demand interpreter services are often available to emergency medical services (EMS) clinicians, utilization may be limited by device accessibility, workflow barriers, and clinician adoption. Our objective was to evaluate whether implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with increased utilization of virtual interpreter services during prehospital care.

Methods: We conducted an observational retrospective pre-post cohort study of virtual interpreter service utilization within a large multistate Midwest EMS agency. On June 1, 2025, the agency issued smartphones (Apple iPhone 16, ∼6 ounces) to all clinicians, providing continuous access to virtual audio and video interpreter services (LanguageLine Solutions). Previously, interpreter services were accessed using large Toughbook laptops (∼6.1 pounds). Interpreter utilization was compared between pre-implementation (October 30, 2024, to May 31, 2025) and post-implementation (June 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025) periods. Interpreter requests per 100 encounters were compared using rate ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

Results: Interpreter requests increased from 104 pre-implementation (0.19 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.15-0.23) to 326 post-implementation (0.57 per 100 encounters, 95% CI: 0.51-0.63; RR= 3.04, 95% CI: 2.44-3.79; p < 0.001). Audio requests increased from 68 calls (0.12 per 100 encounters) to 271 calls (0.47 per 100 encounters; RR = 3.86, 95% CI: 2.96-5.03; p < 0.001). Video requests increased from 36 calls (0.06 per 100 encounters) to 55 calls (0.10 per 100 encounters), although the observed increase did not reach statistical significance (RR= 1.48, 95% CI: 0.97-2.25; p = 0.066). The most commonly requested languages were Spanish (n = 153, 36%), Somali (n = 146, 34%), and Arabic (n = 41, 10%).

Conclusions: Implementation of agency-issued lightweight clinician-carried smartphones was associated with a threefold increase in virtual interpreter utilization. This increase was driven primarily by audio interpretation, while the observed increase in video utilization did not reach statistical significance. These findings suggest that improving point-of-care accessibility of interpreter services through lightweight mobile devices may facilitate greater utilization during prehospital encounters with patients with LEP.

item.title: JAMA Intern Med: Removing Race From Standardized Mortality Ratio Risk Adjustment in Dialysis Care Quality Measurement
item.description:
Importance: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) adjusts for race and ethnicity when calculating and publicly reporting standardized mortality ratios (SMRs) of dialysis facilities. In July 2025, CMS removed race, ethnicity, and related demographic fields from the End-Stage Renal Disease Medical Evidence Report-the primary data source for race and ethnicity in SMR risk adjustment.

Objective: To evaluate how removing race and ethnicity from SMR calculations is associated with facility-level performance, particularly among facilities serving high proportions of patients with social risk factors.

Design, setting, and participants: In this cross-sectional study using the US Renal Data and Renal Management Information Systems, data from dialysis facilities in the US during the period of January 2017 to December 2020 were analyzed from October 2025 to January 2026. Facilities were categorized into quintiles based on the proportion of incident patients who were non-Hispanic Black, Hispanic, living in highly disadvantaged neighborhoods, or uninsured or Medicaid-covered at dialysis initiation. A composite social risk score classified facilities as being in the highest quintile of none, 1, or at least 2 of these characteristics.

Exposure: Race and ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and insurance coverage proportions of patients.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcomes were change in facility-level SMR values and rankings after the removal of race and ethnicity from risk adjustment.

Results: Among 6895 dialysis facilities, 6220 (90.2%) were for profit, and 1588 (23.0%) had the highest social risk score of 2 or higher. With race-inclusive adjustment, the mean (SD) SMR among facilities with the lowest social risk was 0.93 (0.39), compared with 1.03 (0.42) among facilities with the highest social risk (difference, 0.10; 95% CI, 0.09-0.12). After removing race and ethnicity, this difference was nearly eliminated to -0.002 (95% CI, -0.02 to 0.01). A total of 1259 facilities (21.6%) with high social risk improved in SMR ranking after race exclusion, compared with 236 facilities (1.9%) with low social risk (difference, 19.7; 95% CI, 18.4-20.9 percentage points). Facilities serving the highest proportion of non-Hispanic Black patients experienced the greatest gains, with 26.6% improving SMR performance, compared with 4.7% among all other facilities (difference, 21.9; 95% CI, 20.5-23.3 percentage points).

Conclusions and relevance: Results of this cross-sectional study suggest that removing race and ethnicity from SMR risk adjustment substantially altered publicly reported mortality performance among dialysis facilities, with the largest changes among facilities serving larger proportions of Black patients. These findings suggest that excluding race and ethnicity from SMR risk adjustment may meaningfully shift performance comparisons in favor of facilities serving populations with greater social risk.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Multilevel Mobility Intervention and Life-Space Mobility in Older Hospitalized Medical Patients: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Low mobility is common during an acute hospitalization and is associated with adverse outcomes, such as loss of independence and death. Previous interventions that were successful in increasing hospital mobility required resources that are not available in everyday clinical practice, limiting their scalability.

Objective: To assess whether the theory-informed Intervention to Increase Mobility in Older Hospitalized Medical Patients (INTOMOB) improves life-space mobility at 30 days in older hospitalized medical patients.

Design, setting, and participants: This is a multicenter, parallel, partially blinded, cluster randomized clinical superiority trial, with randomization at the hospital ward level and 180-day follow-up. Patients were recruited between October 2023 and January 2025 at acute general internal medicine wards of 3 Swiss hospitals. Main eligibility criteria were age 60 years or older, living in the community, and planned hospital stay 3 or more days.

Intervention: The intervention was compared with standard of care and included booklets and videos for patients, health care professional training, and posters in the wards.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was life-space mobility at 30 days, a measure of how far and often a person moves within their environment, from bedroom to beyond their town (range, 0-120 points, with higher scores denoting greater mobility). Secondary outcomes included physical activity during hospitalization, new institutionalizations (ie, transition to nursing home), and quality of life. For time-to-event outcomes, Cox models with cluster-robust SEs were used. Multinomial logistic regression with robust SEs was used for categorical outcomes.

Results: Of 1334 eligible patients, 383 (median [IQR] age, 75 [68 to 81] years; 234 male [61.1%]) agreed to participate and were randomized to 12 clusters (183 patients [47.8%] in the intervention group and 200 patients [52.2%] in the control group). The primary outcome was available for 327 patients (85.4%). The median (IQR) length of stay was 5 (3 to 7) days. Life-space mobility at 30 days was not significantly different between control and intervention groups (adjusted difference, 0.67 points; 95% CI, -4.35 to 5.68 points). There were no serious adverse events potentially related to the intervention. There was no consistent statistically significant difference in any other secondary outcomes.

Conclusions and relevance: The INTOMOB intervention did not result in a significantly improved short-term life-space mobility or other clinical outcomes. However, the feasibility of the INTOMOB intervention provides a foundation for future mobility interventions aiming to improve both effectiveness and applicability in everyday clinical practice.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05639231; Swiss National Clinical Trial Portal Identifier: SNCTP000005259.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Study Rationale, Enrollment Characteristics, and Central Review of Clinical Stage: The INTACT Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Trimodality therapy (TMT) is an established bladder-preservation approach for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). Accurate clinical staging remains challenging and may affect patient selection, trial design, and interpretation of outcomes.

Objective: To describe the design, accrual, and baseline characteristics of the Phase III Randomized Trial of Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy With or Without Atezolizumab in Localized Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (INTACT) trial and evaluate agreement between site-reported and centrally reviewed clinical stage and the prevalence of high-risk disease features.

Design, setting, and participants: INTACT is a phase 3 randomized clinical trial that enrolled patients with localized MIBC (stage cT2-T4aN0M0) at 136 US sites between April 2019 and March 2025. For this analysis, 243 patients with available source documentation were randomly selected by the SWOG Statistical Center for central clinical staging review.

Interventions: Patients were randomized to physician's choice of concurrent chemotherapy (cisplatin, gemcitabine, or 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin C) and radiotherapy (bladder only or small pelvis; 64-64.8 Gy), with or without atezolizumab (1200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks for 9 cycles).

Main outcomes and measures: The trial's primary end point is 3-year bladder-intact event-free survival, which is not reported in this analysis. Outcomes for the present analysis included trial accrual, clinical stage distribution, agreement between site-reported stage and the initial independent central reviewer, and prevalence of predefined high-risk features (carcinoma in situ, unilateral hydronephrosis, or tumor >5 cm). Agreement was assessed using Cohen κ and directional disagreement using the McNemar test.

Results: Among 485 randomized patients, the median (IQR) age was 73.8 (37.6-93.6) years, 384 (79.2%) were male, 16 (3.3%) were Asian, 33 (6.8%) were Black, and 419 (86.4%) were White. Site investigators classified 398 (82.1%) as stage cT2 and 87 (17.9%) as stage cT3 or T4a. Among 243 patients selected for central review, 201 (82.7%) had site-reported stage cT2 disease and 42 (17.3%) had stage cT3 or T4a disease. Agreement between site-reported stage and the initial independent central reviewer was moderate (κ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.34-0.62). Of 201 site-reported stage cT2 cases, 24 (11.9%) were assigned stage cT3 or T4a by the central reviewer; of 42 site-reported stage cT3 or T4a cases, 15 (35.7%) were assigned stage cT2. Among patients with site-reported stage cT2 disease, 113 (56.2%) had at least 1 high-risk feature. Overall, 155 of 243 patients (63.8%) had at least 1 high-risk feature.

Conclusions and relevance: In this phase 3 randomized clinical trial, a pragmatic design facilitated accrual of 485 patients to a US bladder-preservation trial. Clinical staging showed moderate agreement between site investigators and independent central review, and more than half of patients classified as stage cT2 had additional high-risk features. These findings support standardized collection of clinical staging and high-risk disease characteristics in future bladder-preservation trials.

Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03775265.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Nationwide Assessment of Trends, Characteristics, and Outcomes of Pregnancy for Cancer Survivors
item.description:
Importance: Cancer survivors are individuals with a diagnosis of malignant neoplasm, either living with (ie, current cancer survivors) or free of (ie, past cancer survivors) cancer. As the prevalence of cancer survivors of reproductive age increases worldwide, assessment of pregnancy characteristics and outcomes among past cancer survivors is important.

Objective: To assess the temporal trends, clinical and obstetric characteristics, and maternal morbidity at delivery among current and past cancer survivors.

Design, setting, and participants: This nationwide cross-sectional study used National Inpatient Sample data for hospital deliveries from 2016 to 2023. Analyses were conducted from April to May 2026.

Exposure: A prior or current diagnosis of cancer at hospital delivery, with individuals classified as being a past cancer survivor, a current cancer survivor, or an individual without a cancer diagnosis.

Main outcome and measure: The primary outcome was severe maternal morbidity at delivery, assessed with multivariable generalized linear models with a Poisson distribution.

Results: Among 28 360 443 hospital deliveries, there were 106 740 (0.4%) hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors, 21 975 (<0.1%) for current cancer survivors, and 28 231 728 (99.5%) without a cancer diagnosis. The median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 33 (29-36), 32 (27-36), and 29 (25-33) years among past cancer survivors, current cancer survivors, and individuals without a cancer diagnosis, respectively. During the 8-year study period, hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors increased from 30.1 to 45.6 per 10 000 hospital deliveries (average annual percentage change [AAPC] = 6.3% [95% CI, 5.1%-7.9%]), whereas hospital deliveries for current cancer survivors were unchanged (7.0 to 7.4 per 10 000 hospital deliveries; AAPC = 0.2% [95% CI, -2.8% to 3.7%]). Most hospital deliveries (57.6%) for past cancer survivors were full-term, whereas only 39.6% were full-term for current cancer survivors. Compared with the no cancer group, the severe maternal morbidity rate was higher for the past cancer survivor group (11.9 vs 6.8 per 1000 hospital deliveries; adjusted incidence rate ratio [IRR], 1.45 [95% CI, 1.37-1.53]) and for the current cancer survivor group (48.2 vs 6.8 per 1000 hospital deliveries; adjusted IRR, 3.80 [95% CI, 3.58-4.04]), including the inpatient maternal mortality rate during the hospital delivery admission (273.0 vs 7.0 per 100 000 hospital deliveries; adjusted IRR, 14.24 [95% CI, 10.87-18.66]).

Conclusions and relevance: In this US cross-sectional study, the prevalence of hospital deliveries for past cancer survivors increased from 2016 to 2023, and severe maternal morbidity was increased at delivery for past and current cancer survivors. These findings support the importance of preconception evaluation for cancer survivors and early referral to tertiary care centers with multidisciplinary teams, as currently recommended by multiple organizations.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Neighborhood Exposure to Firearm Violence and Measures of Psychosocial Distress
item.description:
Importance: Exposure to firearm violence is believed to have substantial indirect health effects among those who experience and witness it.

Objective: To assess whether neighborhood firearm violence is associated with psychological and behavioral outcomes.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study links geocoded, individual-level data from adults participating in the 2021 and 2022 California Health Interview Surveys, a state-representative survey conducted annually by the UCLA Center for Health Policy Research linked to shooting events near interviewees' home from the Gun Violence Archive. Data analysis was performed from August to October 2025.

Exposure: Any shooting event occurring within 500 m of interviewees' households within the past 12 months (January 1, 2020, and December 31, 2022). Sensitivity analyses included any fatal shooting, any shooting within the past 2 months, and more than 1 shooting event.

Main outcome and measures: Primary outcomes were self-reported worry about experiencing firearm violence, feeling unsafe in one's neighborhood, heavy substance use, and psychological distress. Survey-adjusted multivariable Poisson regression models assessed the association between the exposure and each outcome.

Results: Among the 45 916 adults interviewed (mean [SD] age, 48.2 [18.7] years; 26 077 [51.8%] female), 6289 (17.2%, weighted) had a shooting occur near their home; there were no missing data. Polysubstance use was positively associated with most exposures, with the highest incident rate ratios (IRRs) among those experiencing a recent shooting in their neighborhood within the past 2 months (IRR, 1.41; 95% CI, 1.18-1.68) and those experiencing more than 1 shooting (IRR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.14-1.55). The highest magnitude associations for each exposure were observed with the outcome of feeling unsafe in one's neighborhood among those experiencing a recent shooting event (IRR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.52-1.97) or more than 1 shooting (IRR, 2.36; 95% CI, 2.17-2.56). All exposures had a positive association with worry about experiencing firearm violence, with IRRs of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.04-1.24) for those experiencing any shooting to 1.28 (95% CI, 1.13-1.43) for those experiencing more than 1 shooting in the past 12 months.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of the association between firearm violence and self-reported psychosocial distress, exposure to neighborhood firearm violence was associated with a range of outcomes that may affect people's perceptions of their safety and could potentially contribute to negative coping behaviors, such as substance use.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Sudden Deaths From Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage and Proximity to Neurosurgical Tertiary Care
item.description:
Importance: A substantial proportion of deaths due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) occur without admission to neurosurgical units. Whether this proportion varies by geographic region is unclear.

Objective: To determine the proportion of SAH deaths without neurosurgical unit admission across hospital districts in 2 high-income countries.

Design, setting, and participants: This retrospective, population-based cohort study used 2 externally validated nationwide administrative data collections in all 41 hospital districts and 10 neurosurgical units in Finland and New Zealand from January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2017. Participants included all hospitalized and fatal nonhospitalized cases with SAH. Data were analyzed from July 1, 2024, to September 7, 2026.

Exposures: Hospital district of residence and its distance to the designated neurosurgical referral center, grouped into 4 zones.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was the death-based proportion of all 30-day deaths after SAH that occurred without neurosurgical unit admission (prehospital deaths plus deaths within 30 days after admission to a nonneurosurgical unit divided by all 30-day deaths from SAH). This proportion was estimated across 41 hospital districts and demographic groups, with age- and sex-adjusted risk ratios (RRs) and 95% CIs.

Results: A total of 12 912 patients with SAH (7856 in Finland and 5056 in New Zealand; median age, 58 [IQR, 49-69] years; 7924 [61.4%] women) were included. Of all 5418 SAH deaths, 3819 (70.5%) occurred without neurosurgical unit admission: 2203 of 3114 (70.7%) in Finland (interdistrict range, 403 of 644 [62.6%] to 5 of 5 [100%]) and 1616 of 2304 (70.1%) in New Zealand (interdistrict range, 111 of 190 [58.4%] to 22 of 23 [95.7%]). Compared with districts containing a neurosurgical unit (1723 of 2602 [66.2%]), the death-based proportions were higher in close-distance (1-130 km; 796 of 1129 [70.5%]; RR, 1.07 [95% CI, 1.02-1.12]), middle-distance (131-157 km; 469 of 599 [78.3%]; RR, 1.18 [95% CI, 1.12-1.24]), and far-distance (158-371 km; 831 of 1088 [76.4%]; RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 1.10-1.20]) zones. This proportion increased by 6.7% (95% CI, 4.9%-8.5%) for each additional 100 km to a neurosurgical unit. The proportions decreased in both countries over time.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cohort study of 12 912 patients with SAH, most deaths occurred without neurosurgical unit admission, and this proportion increased with distance to the neurosurgical referral center. Prevention and early management outside tertiary care may therefore warrant priority in reducing SAH mortality.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Resistance Exercise Training for Depressive Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression Analysis
item.description:
Importance: Resistance exercise training (RET) has established antidepressant effects compared with inactive control conditions; however, its effects vs active comparisons remain unclear.

Objective: To quantify the association of RET efficacy with active and inactive comparisons for depressive symptoms and explore variability across moderators.

Data sources: Published articles were identified using Google Scholar, MEDLINE, PubMed, Web of Science, and PsycInfo from inception to July 7, 2025.

Study selection: Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) with at least 3 weeks of RET or any non-RET comparison and a validated depressive symptom measure at baseline and at least 3 weeks were included. Active comparisons were aerobic exercise training, relaxation, flexibility, mind-body exercise, nutrition, education, advice or attention, mixed activities, and balance exercises. Inactive comparisons were no treatment, waiting lists, and continued usual care.

Data extraction and synthesis: Three reviewers independently extracted data. Meta-regression was used to test moderators, including primary moderators (age, sex, mental health status, RET duration, intensity, concealed allocation). Study quality was assessed using a modified Detsky scale.

Main outcomes and measures: All available associations of RET vs comparison conditions with depressive symptoms were quantified from baseline to at least 3 weeks. Random-effects models were used.

Results: Across 80 RCTs including 6123 participants (2880 participants [47.0%] in RET groups and 3243 [53.0%] in non-RET comparison groups; mean [SD] age, 57 [16] years; 3412 female [67.1%]), the number of effect sizes examined was 176; 57 RCTs enrolled participants with an illness. Resistance exercise training was associated with a significant, heterogenous, small-magnitude antidepressant effect size (Δ = 0.32 [95% CI, 0.25-0.39]; z = 9.31; P < .001) across all comparisons. The effect size was larger vs inactive comparisons (Δ = 0.54 [95% CI, 0.39-0.68]; z = 7.22; P < .001) than active comparisons (Δ = 0.21 [95% CI, 0.14-0.27]; z = 6.20; P < .001). Versus active comparisons, RET was associated with a significant, heterogenous, small-magnitude antidepressant effect size, with larger effect sizes among participants with a mental illness (Δ = 0.40 [95% CI, 0.29-0.50]) vs without a mental illness (Δ = 0.11 [95% CI, 0.04-0.18]). Versus inactive comparisons, RET was associated with a significant, heterogenous, moderate-magnitude antidepressant effect size, with larger effect sizes for all-female cohorts (Δ = 0.87 [95% CI, 0.60-1.14]), RET frequencies of at least 4 days per week (Δ = 0.46 [95% CI, 0.31-0.60]), and session durations of 30 minutes or less (Δ = 1.75 [95% CI, 0.97-2.54]), and smaller effect sizes with concealed allocation (Δ = 0.32 [95% CI, 0.20-0.44]).

Conclusions and relevance: This meta-analysis and meta-regression analysis found that RET was associated with moderate-magnitude, clinically meaningful reductions in depressive symptoms that were greater than other activities with antidepressant benefits, supporting the recommendation of RET in the treatment of depression.

item.title: JAMA Netw Open: Climate Vulnerability, Historical Redlining, and Children's Mental Health Care Use
item.description:
Importance: Structural inequities stemming from historical redlining and environmental injustice have created varying levels of risk among marginalized communities. However, the association of climate risk and structural racism with pediatric mental health care use remains underexplored.

Objectives: To examine associations between climate vulnerability and pediatric mental health care use, and to assess whether these associations vary by historical redlining status.

Design, setting, and participants: This cross-sectional study of children aged younger than 18 years residing in New York State between 2017 and 2022 used all-payer hospital administrative data from the New York State Department of Health. Statistical analysis was conducted from January 2025 through February 2026.

Main outcome and measures: Outcomes included mental health-related emergency department (ED) and outpatient visits identified using International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision-coded mental health diagnosis subtypes (eg, depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder), aggregated at the census-tract level. The primary exposure was climate-specific Climate Vulnerability Index quartiles (where 1 indicates low climate vulnerability and 4 indicates high climate vulnerability). Poisson regression models were conducted to examine associations between Climate Vulnerability Index quartiles and mental health-related health care utilization, including interactions with neighborhood-level redlining status (Home Owners' Loan Corporation grades C/D vs A/B) and subtype-specific analyses. Models adjusted for age, sex, self- or guardian-reported race and ethnicity, and neighborhood-level covariates, with coefficients reported as rate ratios (RRs).

Results: A total of 553 134 mental health-related visits were included (mean [SD] age, 7.2 [5.8] years; 285 526 male [51.6%]). Compared with children living in areas with the lowest climate vulnerability, those living in the highest-vulnerability areas had higher outpatient visit rates (RR, 1.98; 95% CI, 1.72-2.27) and non-statistically significantly higher ED visit rates (RR, 1.14; 95% CI, 0.96-1.35). Associations between high climate vulnerability and mental health-related health care utilization varied by redlining status. In historically redlined neighborhoods, high climate vulnerability was associated with outpatient health care utilization (RR, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.44-1.51; P < .001 for interaction) and, to a lesser extent, ED utilization (RR, 1.06; 95% CI, 1.02-1.09; P < .001 for interaction); in nonredlined neighborhoods high climate vulnerability was associated with lower outpatient health care utilization (RR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.45-0.49; P < .001 for interaction) and not associated with ED utilization (RR, 1.00; 95% CI, 0.93-1.07). Associations also varied across mental health diagnosis subtypes, with higher climate vulnerability associated with increased health care utilization for most diagnosis subtypes.

Conclusions and relevance: In this cross-sectional study of children, residence in historically redlined and climate-vulnerable neighborhoods was associated with higher rates of mental health-related health care utilization. These findings highlight geographic patterns in mental health-related health care utilization that may be relevant to future research on climate preparedness, mental health services, culturally responsive care, and access to services for children experiencing climate-related stressors and structural inequities.

item.title: N Engl J Med: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age
item.category: The New England journal of medicine
item.description:
Background: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking.

Methods: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68.

Results: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group.

Conclusions: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

item.title: Am J Respir Crit Care Med: The Effect of Telemedicine-Based APAP Management on 24-Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure in Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Randomized Clinical Trial
item.category: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
item.description:
Rationale: Telemedicine improves access to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) care, but whether telemedicine-based auto-adjusting positive airway pressure (APAP) management is noninferior to in-person care for the 3-month change in 24-hour mean blood pressure (BP) remains uncertain.

Objectives: To determine whether comprehensive telemedicine-based APAP management is noninferior to standard in-person care in reducing 24-hour mean BP in patients with OSA.

Methods: In this prospective, randomized non-inferiority trial, 344 participants with suspected OSA were randomized 1:1 to telemedicine-based (TM) or in-person (IP) management for 3 months. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in 24-hour mean BP. The prespecified non-inferiority margin was 1.5 mmHg. Secondary outcomes included APAP adherence, patient-centered outcomes and metabolic parameters.

Measurements and main results: Of 344 randomized participants, 256 completed the 3-month follow-up (127 IP and 129 TM). The between-group difference (TM - IP) in the change in 24-hour mean BP was -0.59 mmHg (95% CI, -2.42 to 1.25) in the intention-to-treat analysis and -1.21 mmHg (95% CI, -3.24 to 0.81) in the completer analysis. Both upper confidence limits were below the prespecified 1.5-mmHg non-inferiority margin. No clear evidence of between-group differences was observed in APAP adherence, patient-reported outcomes, or metabolic measures.

Conclusions: Telemedicine-based APAP management was noninferior to in-person management for the 3-month change in 24-hour mean BP, using a prespecified margin of 1.5 mmHg. These findings support telemedicine as a potential alternative delivery model for blood pressure management in patients with OSA.

item.title: JAMA: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial
item.description:
Importance: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed.

Objective: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes.

Design, setting, and participants: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.

Interventions: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention.

Main outcomes and measures: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand.

Results: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events.

Conclusions and relevance: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings.
